31408348abad9f9a: GUA MUSANG, Oct 13 — The absence of accurate numbers of individuals without identification documents poses a challenge for the National Registration Department (NRD) in identifying the Orang Asli and indigenous communities who are still left out of the national registration system.

NRD director-general Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said that his department can only identify these individuals when they come forward to seek JPN services, making it difficult to determine the actual number of those who still do not have identity cards or birth certificates.

He said the issue not only involves the Orang Asli community in Peninsular Malaysia but also the indigenous communities in Sabah and Sarawak, who are believed to still have individuals without identification documents.

“We do not know exactly how many are unregistered, nor do we know how many will attend; however, Alhamdulillah, we have received applications from more than 30 individuals aged 12,” he said at a press conference following the Registration Literacy Programme, held in conjunction with the state-level 78th National Registration Day celebrations, in Pos Balar here yesterday.

He said that NRD is committed to implementing outreach programmes to engage with communities in rural areas, including providing services for first-time identity card applications, identity card replacements, as well as matters related to birth and death certificates.

Badrul Hisham said that continuous efforts are important to ensure that communities in rural areas have access to documentation services, as well as to help address the issue of registration neglect among those communities.
Meanwhile, during the programme, more than 30 Orang Asli children aged 12 in Pos Balar here applied for their identity cards for the first time through the JPN outreach programme today.

Badrul Hisham said that the response to the documentation services provided through the NRD mobile van has been very encouraging, with the local community also taking the opportunity to obtain identity card and birth certificate replacement services.
He said the number of first-time MyKad applications for 12-year-old children is expected to increase as many residents were still queuing to obtain NRD services during the programme.
“For today, we have received more than 30 who are getting their ICs for the first time (12 years old). And if we look at the mobile van, there were still many people queuing,” he said.
He said that the Menyemai Kasih Rakyat (Mekar) programme is part of NRD’s commitment to reach out to communities in rural areas to facilitate their access to identity documents.
In addition to first-time MyKad applications, he said NRD also provides services for replacing identity cards as well as handling matters related to birth and death certificates.
The effort is important to ensure that communities in rural areas have easier access to the registration and documentation services provided by the government. — Bernama
298e4ac03b67f8ee: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor's property market is poised for a defining moment, with the highly anticipated Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) masterplan and blueprint set to be unveiled this December.
RHB Research said the move could unlock fresh value across Iskandar Malaysia and reinforce the region's position as a premier cross-border investment hub.

The unveiling, confirmed at the 2027 Budget, is scheduled to coincide with the annual Singapore-Malaysia Leaders' Retreat, placing the economic zone firmly in the spotlight as both countries deepen bilateral economic cooperation.

The launch will be officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, signalling high-level commitment to the JS-SEZ and its role in driving investment, economic growth and longer-term property demand in Johor.

The rollout will introduce 12 targeted strategic initiatives alongside broad non‑fiscal policy support, designed to cement JS‑SEZ's standing as a leading regional destination for trade, industry, and real estate growth.
RTS DELAY: A BRIEF PAUSE, NOT A SETBACK

RHB Research analyst Loong Kok Wen underscored that the delay to the much-awaited Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link should be viewed as a temporary setback rather than a derailment of the project's long-term growth potential.

While the RTS link will see its public opening pushed back by one to two months to February 2027, the delay reflects rigorous final safety assessments by independent consultants and regulatory approvals from Malaysia's Land Public Transport Agency and Singapore's Land Transport Authority, steps to ensure long‑term reliability.
"Despite the delay, the investment thesis for Iskandar Malaysia has not changed," Loong said in a recent note.
She added that despite the adjustment to the timeline, the core investment thesis for Iskandar Malaysia remains fully intact.
TOP PLAYS POISED TO DELIVER

Loong said leading developers and industrial‑focused property groups are already seeing strong market momentum, with demand driven by cross‑border connectivity, industrial expansion, and new township growth.
Eco World Development Group Bhd (EcoWorld) stands out with exceptional take‑up across its industrial portfolio.

Loong said Eco Business Parks I, II and III, plus the high‑tech Quantum Edge development, have drawn robust interest from local and international manufacturers, industrial operators, and fast‑growing data centre investors, positioning Johor as a digital and advanced manufacturing hub.

KSL Holdings Bhd has also demonstrated sharp buyer appetite with its Riveria Garden township, launched earlier in 2026 and already fully sold, underscoring enduring demand for well‑located, large‑scale residential communities.

Meanwhile, Loong said Mah Sing Group Bhd is gearing up to introduce MS Industrial Park @ Kulai in late 2026 or early 2027, tapping into surging demand for modern industrial space near key transport links.
UEM Sunrise Bhd, Sunway Bhd and other key Iskandar Malaysia players also remain well‑placed to capture sustained value growth as JS‑SEZ policies and infrastructure roll out, she said.
WHAT THIS MEANS FOR INVESTORS
With the masterplan now weeks away, policy frameworks taking shape, and the RTS link on the horizon, Johor is moving beyond promise to delivery.

For homebuyers, industrial tenants, and investors alike, this is far more than a single infrastructure project, it is the building of a shared economic zone that will tie Malaysia and Singapore closer together for decades to come.
The fundamentals have not shifted The region's long‑term appeal, amplified by policy backing, cross‑border integration, and diversified growth, continues to strengthen.

39e5a4b342ce774e: OCTOBER 13 — Budget 2027, tabled on October 9, sets out substantial financial commitments to Malaysia’s economic and social priorities.

The Finance Ministry’s Fiscal Outlook estimates federal expenditure at RM459.8 billion, excluding the contingency reserve. Yet the budget’s value will depend on how that money becomes accessible services and better living conditions.
The headline allocation begins the assessment; it cannot settle whether policy will work.
The priorities deserve fair consideration.

The proposed RM16 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) is intended to ease pressure on household finances. Development expenditure is projected at RM83 billion, while the fiscal deficit is projected at 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product in 2027. Policymakers are attempting to balance social protection and development with fiscal discipline, amid competing demands on public funds.

The government also announced a minimum wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June 2027, with exemptions for micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million. That qualification matters to workers’ expectations. As of October 12, these announcements remain commitments for the coming year. Their effects must be established after implementation.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Budget 2027’s success will depend on how effectively public spending translates into better services, stronger household finances and improved living conditions. — Bernama pic

A useful assessment separates four stages. Inputs comprise funding, personnel and other resources. Outputs are the assistance, facilities and services actually delivered. Outcomes are the resulting changes, such as shorter treatment waits, higher real incomes or better employment opportunities. Long-term impact concerns sustainable development, social mobility and narrower gaps in opportunity across regions and generations.

A clinic illustrates the distinction. Its allocation is an input; a completed, operating facility is an output. Better access to effective treatment is an outcome. If staffing, medicines and patient transport are poorly coordinated, the building’s benefits may be limited. This is an implementation risk to manage, rather than a claim that any particular project has failed.

For households, the relevant test is purchasing power. The Department of Statistics Malaysia recorded inflation of 1.9 per cent in August 2026. This aggregate cannot precisely represent every family’s experience because spending patterns differ. Income gains must be considered alongside food, rent, transport and childcare costs. A larger nominal income does not by itself establish greater financial security.

Equal assistance payments can also produce unequal net benefits. A recipient facing expensive travel or lost daily earnings to obtain support may retain less of its value. Evaluation should therefore include the cost of accessing assistance, including time. Comparing urban and rural communities, and different regions, requires attention to recipients’ experience as well as money disbursed.

Wage growth must also be considered alongside productivity and small businesses’ ability to remain viable. In its Budget 2027 commentary, Bank Negara Malaysia emphasised that productivity, innovation and investment should strengthen alongside rising incomes. Wage policy should be assessed through compliance, real earnings, working hours and hiring. Access to finance and training, together with timely payments to small suppliers, also matters.
Three practical improvements could strengthen accountability without presuming that more spending is the answer.

First, government should strengthen public reporting through an accessible Budget 2027 implementation scorecard. This can build on existing mechanisms. Federal expenditure estimates already contain performance indicators, including ambulance response and patient waiting times for the Health Ministry. The additional value would come from connecting such measures to allocations, current progress and agency responsibility in one understandable presentation.

For each major initiative, the scorecard should identify the responsible agency, baseline, target and delivery timetable. Disbursement rates, actual beneficiary numbers and profiles, geographical coverage and delivery times measure implementation. Changes in service quality, income stability or ability to meet essential needs help measure outcomes. Presenting these separately would prevent rapid spending from being mistaken for improved welfare.

Coverage should be measured against the estimated eligible population, using individuals or households as appropriate to each programme. A large beneficiary count can conceal people whom the programme has yet to reach. Rewarding numbers alone risks encouraging agencies to prioritise applicants who are easiest to contact. Reporting should therefore explain efforts to overcome access barriers while protecting personal information.

Quarterly delivery updates could use existing administrative records, with outcomes assessed over suitable periods. Indicators should be selective enough to avoid burdening frontline staff. Income changes also reflect wider economic conditions, so a simple comparison before and after assistance cannot establish the programme’s contribution. Evaluation methods and data limitations should be explained openly.

Second, agencies should coordinate data and application procedures. Updated information on income, dependants and eligibility could reduce duplication and exclusion. Data-based decisions nevertheless need clear appeals channels and assistance in person for applicants facing digital barriers. Coordination should make correcting a record easier, with agencies resolving discrepancies rather than sending applicants repeatedly between counters.

Third, programmes involving substantial expenditure or significant implementation risks should face independent scrutiny through existing audit and parliamentary channels. Reviews should examine procurement transparency and efficiency, service quality and the cost of achieving results. Where targets are missed, agencies should publish the reasons, the unit responsible and a timetable for corrective action. Findings should inform programme redesign before expansion.

Fiscal discipline also requires provision for maintenance, staffing and operating costs throughout a project’s life. New facilities create obligations beyond construction. Development spending should therefore be assessed against the capacity to keep those facilities functioning, so that today’s decisions do not leave unplanned costs for users or future budgets.

Budget 2027 should ultimately be judged by evidence connecting public commitments to benefits people can actually obtain. Numbers remain essential to determining what Malaysia can afford and holding institutions accountable. Policy effectiveness depends on whether those resources improve services, widen opportunity and strengthen household security. Fiscal responsibility, effective governance and public welfare reinforce one another when spending decisions remain answerable to the lives they are intended to improve.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.
873258d6b6406e75: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The national men’s sepak takraw squad, the Golden Tigers, have received a windfall of RM160,000 after winning one gold and one silver at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games.

The Malaysian Sepak Takraw Association (PSM) distributed the reward to 12 players and two coaches, who also received gold bars and shopping vouchers from strategic partner Telekom Malaysia (TM Group).

PSM president Datuk Mohd Sumali Reduan said the governing body was unwilling to sit back and wait solely for the government’s reward scheme, opting instead to raise funds on its own to recognise the players’ sacrifices at the quadrennial Games.
“I think this is the first time in the history of Malaysian sepak takraw that players are being recognised with a fairly substantial sum.

“While we know that KBS (Ministry of Youth and Sports) and MSN (National Sports Council) provide rewards and incentives under SHAKAM (the National Sports Victory Reward Scheme), my responsibility and that of the entire PSM committee is to decide that we too must take the initiative. Even if it is not much, we give it to them,” he said.
He said this after the National Sepak Takraw Squad appreciation ceremony in the capital last night.

Among those present were Olympic Council of Malaysia deputy president Datuk Nur Azmi Ahmad, MSN director-general Jefri Ngadirin and National Sports Institute chief executive officer Dr P. Vellapandian.
Mohd Sumali said the allocation was based on the association’s current means and did not rule out the possibility of the amount increasing in the future.
Meanwhile, national chief server Mohammad Syahir Mohd Rosdi described the incentive as an unexpected blessing, given that the association had no formal obligation to provide cash rewards.

“Maybe each person gets about RM10,000 if it is divided. After this, we will receive further incentives under SHAKAM, but we do not yet know the amount. As players, we are grateful and proud to receive this from PSM and TM,” he said.

The national men’s sepak takraw squad ended a 36-year wait for the team regu gold medal after defeating traditional rivals Thailand 2-0 in the final, while also clinching silver in the men’s regu event after losing 0-2 to them. — Bernama
43ab1317f051c79e: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 13 — Meta on Monday unveiled two new “frontier” artificial intelligence models called Wonder and Wonder Full, which the company claims perform at a level comparable to that of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude.
“Muse Spark was our first family of models, and now Muse Wonder is a much larger and more advanced class of models that brings us to the frontier,” CEO Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X.

Zuckerberg has pushed Meta to compete with leading AI labs, particularly OpenAI and Anthropic over the past year or so amid a race to win over customers and diversify beyond advertising, which has historically been its main source of revenue.
In June 2025, the company made a US$14 billion (RM57.2 billion) investment in Scale AI, an AI startup based in San Francisco, and poached its co-founder Alexandr Wang as part of the deal.
Zuckerberg subsequently made Wang the company’s chief AI officer overseeing its newly formed division called Superintelligence Labs.
Meta launched its Spark model in April, marking a departure from its open-source model known as Llama, which lagged behind the rest of the industry.
The new models can soon be used in Meta’s new personal agent app, known as Muse, for paid subscribers only.
Wonder is “our largest and most capable model yet” and “rivals the big (boys),” Wang posted on X, presumably referring to leading labs OpenAI and Anthropic.

In a blog post, Meta touted so-called benchmarking data from an independent firm called Artificial Analysis that appears to show that Meta’s newest Wonder models outperform its own previous models, Spark, as well as various models developed by Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.
Artificial Analysis’s website shows that Wonder is also among the most expensive models.
Meta has committed billions towards competing in the global race to dominate AI, despite growing concerns about safety and security.
In July, the Facebook and Instagram maker said its spending on AI-related investments could reach US$145 billion this year.
The company has more than 3.6 billion daily active users around the world.
Speeding up
In its early years, Facebook was known to operate under a philosophy of “move fast and break things,” but more recently, Zuckerberg implied Meta would balance safety with speed.
“Meta delayed shipping Muse for several months to focus on safety and security. We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would,” Zuckerberg posted on X last month.
In August, Meta launched Muse Code, a product intended to compete with similar automated coding tools offered by OpenAI and Anthropic.
Then in September, it launched an agentic app called Muse. Agentic software can autonomously perform specific tasks such as coding, research, shopping, booking reservations or shopping.

At its annual developer conference Connect last month, Meta also revealed a new handheld AI hardware product called Muse Charm that allows users to interact with their Muse agent separately from a smartphone.
Developers have been racing to design agentic apps that will capture users’ attention, time and wallets. AI-powered hardware remains an elusive goal for the industry as well.
While Silicon Valley heavyweights OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta dominate the landscape, young startups like Instinct are also becoming breakout hits.
Zuckerberg sped up Muse’s launch due to Instinct’s popularity, the New York Times reported.
Some competitors have called for an industry-wide slowdown to address and mitigate safety concerns.

In September, Zuckerberg was one of six American tech executives to sign what President Donald Trump described as a “morally binding” commitment to build adequate safeguards around ever more advanced AI models.
Executives from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and Nvidia also signed the agreement but there is no consensus among politicians or industry leaders around how to best move forward.

Leaders at Anthropic, OpenAI and Google have encouraged “pacing” - or slowing down — development after models created by all three were found to have escaped their testing environments or taken actions without authorisation.

“We will slow down as much as necessary in order to make sure that every successive AI technology that we release is actually safe,” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told the United Nations last month. — AFP

3840720080c59238: LONDON: British consumers kept a lid on spending in September, with much of their extra outlay going on fuel, while warm weather helped pubs but hurt clothing sales, according to surveys published on Tuesday.

The British Retail Consortium (BRC) trade body said its total retail sales measure rose by 1.3 per cent compared with a year ago, picking up from 0.7 per cent in August but below its 12-month average of 1.5 per cent.
A separate survey from Barclays, based on consumer card spending data, showed a 2.0 per cent annual increase in September, slowing from August's 2.1 per cent rise.
It pointed to a rise in households' confidence around their finances but also some nerves ahead of Finance Minister John Healey's budget on October 28.
Here are the key points from the two surveys:
• The BRC said food sales were up by 2.5 per cent while non-food sales edged up by 0.3 per cent.

• Health and beauty had its strongest month of the year so far and toys were boosted by Pokemon's 30th anniversary products, but clothing and footwear had a weak month due to unseasonably warm weather.

• "Retail sales growth remained subdued in September as households are still cautious with their spending ahead of expected rises in household bills and taxes," said BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson.
• Barclays said essential spending was up by 2.5 per cent, driven by a 17.3 per cent jump in fuel spending after diesel prices hit record highs, while non-essential spending edged up by 1.8 per cent.
• Bars, pubs and clubs reported a 3.8 per cent rise in spending, their fourth straight month of growth, as summer weather extended through most of September

• Barclays' measure of confidence in household finances rose to a seven-month high of 67 per cent, but 68 per cent of consumers said they were concerned about the budget's impact on their finances and 30 per cent said they were cutting back on non-essential spending.
• The BRC survey covered the period of Aug 30-Oct 3, while the Barclays spending data was Aug 22-Sept 24
91f2d68fd01e3ce1: SINGAPORE, Oct 13 — A 52-year-old man was arrested by the police after he assaulted two Land Transport Authority’s (LTA) active mobility enforcement officers (AMEOs) during a recent enforcement operation.
LTA said in a Facebook post on Monday (Oct 12) that the incident, involving a male rider suspected of using a non-compliant device, happened in Ang Mo Kio.
The man was arrested for voluntarily causing hurt to deter a public servant from his duty.
“LTA has zero tolerance for violence or abuse against our officers. We will work closely with the police to ensure that such acts are dealt with sternly,” it said.
“We remind all members of the public to cooperate with our officers and comply with their instructions during enforcement checks.”
In response to AsiaOne’s queries, the police said that the man was arrested on Oct 8.
Investigations into the offence – which carries a penalty of up to seven years’ jail, a fine, or caning – are ongoing.
Meanwhile, AMEOs detected a total of 503 offences during enforcement operations in September.
According to LTA, 70 devices were impounded.
Based on the photos shared by LTA, these operations took place in the vicinity of Bukit Panjang, Balestier and Whampoa.

“We will continue to conduct regular patrols and take firm action against errant users, including those using non-compliant devices and riding on pedestrian overhead bridges to keep our paths safe for everyone,” LTA said. — AsiaOne
84c89881877d9117: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — A local man in his 40s is feared drowned after being reportedly swept away in Sungai Chuah, Kajang, Sunday.

Selangor Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the search and rescue (SAR) operation, which began yesterday, was suspended at 4.30 pm yesterday due to heavy rain and will resume tomorrow.
He said the search was carried out using kayaks and boats, alongside search efforts along the riverbanks.
"The department's K9 tracker dog unit and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel are also involved in locating the victim at the scene," he said in a statement.
JBPM received an emergency call at 5.23 pm yesterday regarding a local man who was swept away in the river before disappearing from view.

The Kajang Fire and Rescue Station dispatched a team that arrived at the scene, located about four kilometres from the station, at 5.29 pm, before the search operation was expanded with assistance from the Shah Alam and Port Klang stations. — Bernama
d3294f4c1e2fc37c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Malaysian Association of Film Exhibitors (MAFE) has welcomed the exemption of entertainment duty for local film screenings and theatre performances in the Federal Territories from January 1, 2027.
The exemption was announced by the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027, on Friday October 9.
In a statement today, MAFE said the move would support Malaysia’s creative industries and strengthen the local film ecosystem.
The association also welcomed the prime minister’s call for similar exemptions to be extended to all states.

MAFE said it would engage with state governments to encourage nationwide adoption of the exemption and work with the Ministry of Communications and the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) to support its implementation.
The association said it remained committed to championing local content and supporting the growth of Malaysia’s film industry.
MAFE, also known as Persatuan Pemamer Filem Malaysia, represents major cinema operators and theatre chains across the country.
ca5f389c6c95debf: OCTOBER 13 — The deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport on October 10, 2026, followed by another attack the next day, marks a dangerous turning point in the fragile relationship between Iran and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
With at least 13 people reportedly killed and more than 300 injured, the assaults demonstrate the Houthis’ willingness to extend Yemen’s conflict into Saudi Arabia’s civilian heartland.
This is no longer merely an internal Yemeni struggle but a regional security crisis with potentially serious consequences for the Middle East and the global economy.
The attacks deserve unequivocal international condemnation.
Civilian airports are not legitimate instruments of political coercion, and targeting passengers and infrastructure cannot be justified.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

This screen grab taken from CCTV footage released by the Saudi Media Ministry on October 11, 2026, shows the moment Riyadh International was hit by a Houthi strike on October 10, 2026. The deadliest strike on Saudi soil in more than a decade killed 12 people at Riyadh’s international airport and wounded hundreds, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to vow on October 11, 2026, a decisive response against Yemen’s Houthis. — Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Media handout pic via AFP

They also expose three weaknesses in the regional security order: the limits of Saudi Arabia’s air defences, the destabilising influence of Iran-aligned armed movements, and the fragility of diplomatic reconciliation between Tehran and the GCC. The third is particularly consequential.
In March 2023, Saudi Arabia and Iran restored diplomatic relations through a China-brokered agreement.
The breakthrough reflected their recognition that permanent confrontation carried enormous economic and strategic costs.
Riyadh needed stability for Vision 2030, while Tehran sought to reduce its isolation and improve relations with neighbouring states.
The Houthis’ continued attacks now threaten that understanding. Iran’s longstanding military and political relationship with the group creates a credibility problem.

Although the Houthis pursue their own objectives and cannot simply be treated as an extension of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), their access to sophisticated missiles and drones has increased their ability to threaten Saudi territory.
This association does not prove that Tehran ordered the latest attacks; such a claim requires credible evidence.
But Iran cannot convincingly present itself as a champion of regional stability while maintaining close ties with actors whose actions endanger its neighbours.
At minimum, it has a diplomatic responsibility to use whatever influence it possesses to prevent further escalation.
The GCC must now consider whether its security environment is deteriorating despite years of engagement. An attack on Riyadh has implications beyond Saudi Arabia.
The UAE has previously experienced attacks attributed to the Houthis, Bahrain remains sensitive to Iranian influence, Kuwait and Qatar favour diplomacy, and Oman has played a key mediating role.
Their differing approaches should not obscure a shared reality: the security of all six GCC states is increasingly interconnected.

The vulnerability of Riyadh’s airport raises concerns about airports, ports, desalination facilities, energy installations and transport networks across the Gulf. Saudi Arabia’s central role in global energy security further internationalises the danger.

With the Strait of Hormuz already exposed to geopolitical disruption, renewed Houthi interference near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could increase shipping costs, insurance premiums, supply-chain uncertainty and inflation across Asia and Europe.
Asean energy-importing economies would be especially vulnerable.

Malaysia, despite being an energy producer, is not insulated from higher logistics costs, imported inflation or market volatility. Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines would face similar pressures. West Asian instability is therefore not a distant concern but a direct economic risk for South-east Asia.
Riyadh’s emerging security cooperation with Türkiye and Pakistan, including the recently announced Mecca defence arrangement, reflects its effort to diversify partnerships.
Condemnation of the attacks by Türkiye, Pakistan, Egypt and Saudi Arabia points to broader diplomatic alignment. Yet deterrence should not be confused with automatic military retaliation.

Effective security cooperation must combine defence, intelligence-sharing, diplomatic pressure and calibrated responses; otherwise, a conflict centred on Yemen could widen into a confrontation involving several powerful states.
Iran must recognise that its relationship with the GCC cannot endure if Iran-aligned movements continue to threaten Gulf civilians.
The October 11 telephone conversation between the Saudi and Iranian foreign ministers, and Tehran’s offer to facilitate Saudi-Yemeni dialogue, provide a possible opening.
But assurances must be matched by tangible de-escalation.
Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, must distinguish defending its sovereignty from launching another prolonged campaign in Yemen.
Military action that deepens civilian suffering without producing a political settlement could perpetuate the insecurity Riyadh seeks to end.
China, having brokered the 2023 rapprochement, has a clear interest in preventing its achievement from unravelling.

The United States and Europe should likewise recognise that Gulf security requires more than additional weapons. It requires a regional framework capable of restraining armed non-state actors and reducing incentives for escalation.
Ultimately, the Houthi attacks have placed Iran–GCC relations under their severest pressure since reconciliation began.
The central test is whether Iran can convert diplomatic influence into meaningful restraint while Saudi Arabia and its partners exercise enough strategic patience to avoid a wider war.
The Gulf cannot afford a permanent cycle of retaliation, and neither can Asean, whose economic security is closely tied to West Asian stability.
The tragedy in Riyadh must become a catalyst for renewed diplomacy, not the beginning of another uncontrollable conflict.
Iran and the GCC have too much to lose from allowing the Houthis to determine the future of their relationship.
* Phar Kim Beng, PhD is the Professor of Asean Studies at International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS).

0fe952999325ec61: SEPANG, Oct 13 — Malaysia will raise the issue of transboundary haze at an Asean foreign ministers’ meeting ahead of the bloc’s 49th Summit in Manila, the Philippines, next month to discuss more effective regional mechanisms to tackle the problem.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the haze issue required special attention as it was not covered by existing Asean mechanisms for natural disasters.
“We already have an Asean mechanism for natural disasters, but haze is not included or classified as a natural disaster.

“So, this will be one of the issues that I will personally raise at the meeting with my counterparts,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here yesterday.

On the latest efforts to extinguish fires in Indonesia, he said his counterpart, Arrmanatha Nasir, had informed him that extremely poor visibility in affected areas was hampering aerial firefighting operations.
“Indonesia has between three to four aeroplanes and 34 helicopters, but they cannot take off because visibility is so poor that it is unsafe for any flights in the affected areas.

“However, they have deployed 60,000 people to work on the ground,” Mohamad said, adding that Indonesia also faced challenges because the fires were located deep inland, water supplies were limited and fires continued to smoulder in peatland areas.
He said cloud-seeding operations could not be carried out in Indonesia at present because suitable cumulonimbus clouds were absent.
Mohamad said Malaysia acknowledged that the Indonesian government was doing its utmost to extinguish the fires and sympathised with the situation facing the country.
However, he said Malaysia hoped its neighbour would take more effective measures as the current situation was adversely affecting the public. — Bernama
a24791efcd5cc0ab: PANAMA CITY: An earthquake of magnitude 6 struck Panama on Monday, the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre (EMSC) said.
"The quake was at a depth of 35km," the EMSC said.

Panama recorded more than 300 aftershocks following Friday's magnitude 7.7 earthquake that damaged hundreds of homes and infrastructure across the country's central provinces, prompting the government to declare a national state of emergency over the weekend.

No deaths were reported, but at least 27 people were injured and nearly 900 homes were damaged, according to emergency authorities, who warned the toll could rise as assessments continue in remote communities.
Among the most affected provinces are Los Santos, Cocle, Veraguas, and Herrera, authorities added.
352ced96796d8926: From Azam Mohd
The 2027 budget raises a question Malaysians rarely ask: who bears responsibility when national promises reach citizens unevenly? The answer cannot rest with Putrajaya alone.

A budget becomes meaningful through state governments, local councils, schools, clinics and businesses. Malaysians should therefore judge this spending plan by whether public institutions can work together across administrative boundaries.

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim tabled a RM460 billion federal budget on Oct 9. The finance ministry projects growth of 4.2% to 5.2% next year, while the fiscal deficit is expected to narrow to 3.3% of gross domestic product.
These forecasts are not guarantees. Their significance depends on what happens after Parliament approves expenditure and ministries begin implementation.
Consider the distance between a federal announcement and a household’s experience.

A parent may welcome education funding but still be confronted with an overcrowded classroom. A patient may hear about health allocations yet encounter long waiting times. A trader may qualify for financing but struggle with permits, infrastructure or inconsistent local enforcement.
Getting things done
None of these difficulties can be resolved by increasing appropriations alone. The missing ingredient is coordination.

Federal ministries design programmes, states control land decisions, and local authorities shape everyday business conditions. When their priorities diverge, public money can purchase activity without producing improvement.

The resulting frustration is often blamed entirely on whichever party governs nationally, although responsibility may be distributed across several institutions. This is particularly important for Sabah and Sarawak, where distance, infrastructure gaps and administrative arrangements complicate delivery. The same principle applies to rural districts in Peninsular Malaysia and densely populated urban neighbourhoods.

Equal allocations do not necessarily create equal access. A credible federal budget must recognise different costs and starting conditions without turning regional needs into partisan bargaining chips.

The 2027 budget also arrives amid uncertainty surrounding the Middle East conflict. Bank Negara Malaysia has announced additional financing support for smaller enterprises facing temporary cash flow pressures. Such measures can help firms survive disruption, but credit cannot repair a blocked supply route or eliminate higher transport costs. Businesses need agencies responsible for financing, logistics and trade facilitation to respond coherently together.
Delivering on promises

Malaysia, therefore, needs a delivery compact between federal and state institutions. For major programmes, the responsible ministry should identify the implementing agencies, milestones and obstacles. State governments should disclose the approvals and infrastructure commitments under their control. Local authorities should report service bottlenecks.
These arrangements would make responsibility visible without assigning every problem one political owner.

Parliament has an important role. Budget debates too often concentrate on announcements and partisan comparisons. Parliamentary committees should instead examine why comparable districts achieve different results with similar resources. Auditors can test whether procurement and implementation follow established rules, while elected representatives can question delays without alleging misconduct.
Poor performance warrants investigation; it is not, by itself, proof of corruption.

There are legitimate objections. Reporting can become bureaucratic, and states may resist federal conditions that intrude upon their constitutional responsibilities. The solution is not another elaborate national dashboard. It is a limited set of jointly agreed service standards, published responsibilities and independent verification, designed around programmes where fragmented authority obstructs delivery.
Out of the political fray

Political competition makes this more urgent. With the next general election approaching, governing parties will claim achievements while opponents highlight shortcomings. Both have legitimate democratic roles.

But citizens should be able to distinguish a policy that failed because of flawed design from one delayed by procurement, staffing, local approvals or unexpected external shocks. That distinction improves accountability rather than shielding ministers from criticism.

A useful starting point would be to select several high impact programmes spanning education, healthcare, small business support and regional connectivity. Publish who is responsible for each stage, invite state participation and review outcomes after implementation begins.
Where cooperation fails, disclose the disagreement and its consequences. Where it succeeds, retain the practice regardless of which coalition controls the relevant government.
The 2027 budget will ultimately reveal whether Malaysia can move beyond a culture in which announcing expenditure is treated as governing.

The country does not lack ambitious public promises. It needs institutions capable of delivering them together, especially when political loyalties differ. Fiscal credibility begins with sound numbers, but public confidence grows when responsibility is shared, visible and impossible to evade.
Azam Mohd is an FMT reader.

23be0a5665a7f0e9: Dunia ini umpama sebuah penjara yang besar dan dipenuhi dengan segala macam hantu. Itu agaknya yang cuba disampaikan oleh Joko Anwar melalui filem arahannya, Ghost in the Cell. Saya tidak tahu apa genre paling tepat untuk filem ini. Komedi seram absurd barangkali tetapi dalam komedi ada serius dan misteri, ada keganasan, ada aksi ala kartun. Semuanya bercampur, mencetuskan kecelaruan. Joko mungkin mahu menyatakan yang hidup ini beginilah, penuh dengan kecelaruan ragam dan identiti. Malah ada babak yang mengarut sehingga saya teringat filem Kung Fu Hustle arahan Stephen Chow.

Filem Ghost in the Cell ini turut menampilkan dua nama dari Malaysia, Bront Palarae yang memegang watak Jefry, seorang pegawai penjara dan Ho Yuhang sebagai Rendra, seorang banduan yang merupakan ketua sindiket dadah. Ho yang lebih dikenali sebagai pengarah filem membawakan watak penjenayah bertubuh kecil tetapi cukup digeruni.

Cerita bermula dengan Dimas (Endy Arfian), seorang wartawan yang dituduh membunuh ketuanya lalu dihumban ke penjara Labuhan Angsana. Di situ dia bertemu pelbagai jenis manusia, termasuk Anggoro (Abimana Aryasatya), seorang banduan yang sering membela orang lain walaupun tindakannya menyebabkan hukuman penjaranya bertambah. Watak Anggoro memperlihatkan satu paradoks. Dia memang pesalah di sisi undang-undang tetapi masih mempunyai rasa kemanusiaan yang tinggi. Sebaliknya, ketua penjara yang diberikan kuasa menjaga undang-undang pula bersifat binatang atau hantu dalam mengejar pangkat dan kedudukan.

Di penjara itu juga ada Tokek (Aming), banduan ganas yang menjadikan keganasan seksual sebagai alat menakutkan orang lain. Dimas yang baru masuk penjara menjadi sasarannya. Tokek mewakili manusia buas dan gemar membuli orang yang lebih lemah. Melihatkan wajahnya sahaja sudah cukup membuat kita menggeletar. Bagaimanapun, dia mati akhirnya setelah gagal mempertahankan diri apabila berhadapan dengan hantu yang ternyata lebih perkasa. Tokek adalah gambaran manusia yang sebenarnya tidaklah kuat mana tetapi hanya berani kerana dia tahu pihak yang dibuli itu sudah sememangnya penakut. Dia memanipulasi keadaan.

Apa yang menarik perhatian saya ialah cara hantu dalam filem ini membunuh mangsanya. Mayat mangsa disusun dan digubah seakan sebuah arca seni. Ini bagai satu metafora yang menarik. Ia tentang kita yang kadangkala menggambarkan keindahan dengan mempergunakan penderitaan orang lain. Arca memanglah cantik dan hebat tetapi ia dibuat menggunakan mayat yang penuh darah dengan isi perut yang terburai, biji mata terkeluar dan sendi yang patah. Manusia begitulah, mempergunakan hidup pihak lain demi mencari keuntungan dengan menjual gossip dan fitnah, hiburan atau berita buruk tentang mereka. Dan kita gembira menikmati keindahannya sebagai bahan tontonan tanpa mempedulikan kesengsaraan di sebaliknya.

Lebih menarik lagi dalam Ghost in the Cell ini ialah hantu yang membunuh itu akan menyerupai mangsanya sendiri ketika menyerang. Ia seolah-olah manusia itu akhirnya dibunuh oleh kejahatan yang terpelihara di dalam tubuhnya sendiri. Hantu bukan datang dari luar, tetapi dari dalam kita sendiri.

Satu lagi watak yang menarik ialah Six (Yoga Pratama), banduan yang tidak berpegang kepada agama tetapi mempunyai kebolehan melihat hantu dan aura manusia. Ini satu lagi paradoks. Selalunya orang alim yang lebih memahami perkara ghaib. Tetapi dalam filem ini, orang yang tidak beragama pula mampu melihat sesuatu yang gagal dilihat oleh orang lain. Saya melihatnya sebagai sindiran, kerana manusia tak kira apa bangsa atau agama pun tetap dikurniakan tuhan dengan kelebihan masing-masing tetapi adakalanya kelebihan yang diberikan itu tidak mampu difahami olehnya sendiri dan dia perlukan bimbingan. Maka itu, banduan alim bernama Wildan (Mike Lucock) diperlukan untuk mentafsir warna-warna aura yang dilihat oleh Six. Wildan tak mampu melihat aura yang keluar dari tubuh manusia seperti mana Six, tetapi dia mempunyai keilmuan untuk mentafsirkannya. Nah! Begitulah tahap manusia dalam memahami, mempercayai dan menghayati sesuatu. Faham, percaya dan menghayati adalah tiga perkara yang cukup besar bezanya.

Di dalam filem ini, tertarik kepada manusia yang mempunyai aura negatif seperti kemarahan dan kebencian. Untuk mengelakkan diri daripada menjadi mangsa, banduan perlu menenangkan fikiran dan mengawal emosi. Ada yang memilih untuk bersembahyang, ada pula yang menari. Sembahyang merupakan ritual yang menghubungkan manusia dengan tuhan, sedangkan menari lazimnya dianggap kegiatan hiburan. Tetapi dalam filem ini, kedua-duanya boleh menghasilkan ketenangan yang diperlukan untuk menghindari hantu. Yang hendak diperlihatkan bukanlah soal cara mana lebih suci atau lebih baik, tetapi bagaimana manusia mencari ketenangan melalui jalan yang berbeza. Maknanya, ketenangan hati itu penting biarpun kita berbeza pegangan. Tetapi di dalam dunia yang bernama penjara, mereka terpaksa mencari apa saja persamaan untuk terus hidup dengan selamat. Untuk selamat, manusia perlu tenang.

Kemudian kita diperkenalkan kepada Prakasa Kitabuming (Arswendy Bening Swara), seorang politikus dan ahli perniagaan berpengaruh yang menjalani hukuman penjara tetapi masih menikmati kemewahan. Dalam penjara yang sama, ada orang yang hidup berhimpit dan terdedah kepada keganasan, sedangkan orang tertentu masih boleh menikmati layanan istimewa. Sepatutnya apabila seseorang dihukum, pangkat dan kedudukannya tidak lagi memberikan keistimewaan. Orang biasa masuk penjara kehilangan kebebasan. Orang berpengaruh masuk penjara masih boleh bermewah-mewahan. Ada pula watak Sapto sebagai Ketua Penjara yang mempunyai cita-cita besar menjadi Menteri sehingga sanggup tersengih-sengih dan melutut demi membodek Prakasa, politikus yang menjadi penghuni penjaranya sendiri.

Sebenarnya hantu itu mahu mencari Prakasa. Hantu mengikut Dimas ketika Dimas meninjau kawasan hutan Kalimantan yang musnah angkara Prakasa. Tetapi, dalam usaha memburu Prakasa ramai yang menjadi korban. Prakasa menemui ajalnya dengan cukup sinis. Dia berhadapan dengan hantu yang menyerupai dirinya ketika muda, ketika dia konon masih seorang pejuang yang mempunyai cita-cita dan prinsip. Dia adalah gambaran pejuang muda yang telah mengkhianati prinsip perjuangannya setelah berada di puncak kuasa. Hantu yang membunuhnya adalah diri mudanya sendiri yang pernah berapi-api berjuang. Rupanya si pejuang ini telah menjadi tawanan kepada pangkat dan kuasa.

Ada satu babak, kita diperlihatkan dengan sekumpulan banduan artis dan selebriti yang diasingkan daripada kumpulan Dimas dan Anggoro. Dialog lucunya ialah ‘rakyat Indonesia lebih mengambil berat nasib artis daripada nasibnya sendiri'. Saya ketawa kerana sindiran itu bukan masalah di Indonesia sahaja. Kita di sini pun sama. Kita boleh bergaduh siapa betul siapa salah bila artis bercerai dan berantak, kita sanggup masukkan duit di dalam akaun bank pempengaruh media sosial yang mengadu perniagaannya bakal melingkup kerana hutang yang membebankan sedangkan apabila sepupu kita hendak menjual dodol buatannya sendiri, kita tak jawab WhatsApp dia langsung. Kita simpati kepada artis yang sedang sakit tetapi jiran sebelah sudah sebulan terlantar di wad, kita tak jenguk pun. Memang kita semua obses dengan artis dan selebriti.

Joko melihat penjara bukan sekadar set penggambaran dan premis penceritaan. Ia adalah dunia. Dunia boleh jadi syurga jika semua manusianya tenang dan damai tetapi dunia boleh jadi sebuah kurungan yang menakutkan jika di dalamnya bercampur antara manusia baik dengan manusia durjana. Di dalam filem ini digambarkan manusia ada yang mahu berkuasa, ada yang mahu dilindungi, ada yang mahu dipuja dan ada yang sekadar mahu terus hidup. Hantu adalah dosa silam yang memburu manusia itu sendiri untuk menghukum jika manusia tersebut masih tidak mahu berubah menjadi insan yang baik. Di tengah-tengah seram, ngeri, takut dan cemas itu kita masih ada ruang untuk ketawa. Sepertinya kita faham bahawa dunia ini hanyalah senda-gurau sementara sahaja.

Memang semenjak dua ini saya sering menulis tentang filem dan teater yang saya tonton. Ini kerana apa yang ingin saya sampaikan dalam tulisan berkenaan kehidupan telah berjaya dipersembahkan oleh mereka dalam bentuk visual. Saya tidak pastilah tafsiran saya menepati apa yang dimaksudkan oleh karyawan asalnya tetapi inilah yang boleh saya kutip untuk dikongsi bersama. Untuk kita renungi kehidupan ini melalui sebuah persembahan kreatif.

Sebuah karya yang sudah dipertontonkan kepada masyarakat tidak semestinya mempunyai satu tafsiran yang wajib dipatuhi. Kita bebas menterjemahnya. Apa yang saya lihat dalam filem ini adalah tentang perangai manusia yang terpenjara akibat menjadi mangsa kepada nafsu buas sendiri. Nafsu manusia memang tak pernah puas. Jika ada peluang untuk naik, manusia akan naik walaupun akan menindas manusia lain. Dari situlah wujudnya dendam dan pembalasan oleh pihak yang teraniaya. Hantu dalam Ghost in the Cell itu muncul pun kerana manusialah yang mengundangnya. Telah kita pelajari di dalam kitab al-Quran, manusia adalah sebaik-baik kejadian dan makhluk terbaik ini jugalah yang sedang menghancur-musnahkan dunia.

b0e58f16f14c4d01: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The ringgit edged higher against the US dollar at the opening, buoyed by optimism surrounding Budget 2027.
At 8 am, the ringgit was up marginally against the greenback to 4.0815/0900 from Monday’s close of 4.0820/0865.

Nevertheless, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam said heightened geopolitical risk in West Asia and expectations of higher US inflation were expected to support the US dollar.
He told Bernama that the situation in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following the missile attacks suggested that the conflict could potentially widen, leading to further disruption to crude oil supplies.

“Brent crude oil prices have already risen by 1.38 per cent to US$106.16 per barrel (RM449.46). b2090f75c2aaa355: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will recommend absorbing contract dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions for the consideration of the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet, in an effort to ensure the future and welfare of these groups are safeguarded.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal would be pursued within a reasonable timeframe, based on the approach previously used to address the issue of contract medical doctors.

“...the first step will be followed by other service schemes, namely dentists and pharmacists as well,” he said when met after appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme titled ‘Realising Budget 2027 With the Health Minister’ last night.
He said the recruitment of dental and pharmacy officers into permanent positions would utilise a new quota separate from the 9,000 permanent medical doctor positions announced under Budget 2027.

The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) was previously reported to have urged the government and MOH to consider permanent appointments for contract dental officers, following the announcement of permanent appointments for medical doctors.

Commenting on reports regarding dental officers whose contracts ended without being renewed, Dzulkefly said MOH would continue to pay attention to their welfare and work experience within the public healthcare system.

In another development, Dzulkefly expressed hope that the Ministry of Finance would consider a request for a seed allocation of approximately RM100 million to strengthen non-communicable disease (NCD) management at the primary healthcare level.
He said the allocation is crucial to enhancing prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment, and continuous control of chronic diseases such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

“Matters related to NCD management are a major component I am bringing into the reforms. In addition to PeKa B40, which received an allocation of RM80 million, managing NCDs from a healthcare perspective is essential to effectively address this chronic disease pandemic.
“It encompasses not only first-stage screening, but also continuous diagnosis, treatment, and control for conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure,” he said.

He added that benchmarking per capita expenditure for NCD management also takes into account practices in countries like Singapore and Indonesia, as well as global trends prioritising primary healthcare services. — Bernama
2635556017974cc7: KUALA LUMPUR: Rows of cars left for months, and even years, along roadsides and in housing areas are not only an eyesore but have also become a persistent problem for residents, prompting calls for firm action by local authorities.
Three local authorities in the Klang Valley recorded a total of 27,117 abandoned vehicles, based on records covering different periods from 2021 to August this year.
Kajang Municipal Council recorded the highest number at 12,290 vehicles, followed by Kuala Lumpur City Hall with 11,001 complaints and Ampang Jaya Municipal Council with 3,826 vehicles.
Vehicles left for too long not only take up parking spaces and obstruct road users but could also pose safety risks and affect the cleanliness of their surroundings.
Abandoned vehicles can pollute soil and water through oil leaks and become breeding grounds for mosquitoes and pests.
Local authorities face difficulties removing abandoned vehicles due to problems tracing owners, inaccurate registration details and lengthy verification and disposal processes.
High repair costs and vehicles that are no longer economical to use are among the factors driving owners to abandon them.
This raises questions about the effectiveness of efforts to tackle the problem more comprehensively.
Kajang Municipal Council recorded 12,290 abandoned vehicles of various types, with the figure showing an upward trend from 2021 to August this year.
Over the past three years, the council received 3,351 complaints related to abandoned vehicles: 1,016 in 2024, 1,216 last year and 1,119 this year.

A council spokesman said Cheras subdistrict recorded the highest number of complaints of abandoned vehicles, particularly in housing areas and around car workshops, with old cars being the most commonly abandoned vehicles.
"Among the factors identified are damaged vehicles, high vehicle repair costs, owning more than one vehicle and vehicles sold without a change of ownership.
"The council will conduct an on-site investigation within 14 days of receiving a complaint, and a warning notice will be affixed to the vehicle.
"Owners are given 14 days to remove the vehicle before towing action is taken," the spokesman said in a written statement to Harian Metro.
According to the council, 2,605 vehicles have been towed, while another 9,685 cases remain unresolved.

The spokesman said the council's main challenges included vehicle owners who had changed addresses, missing vehicle registration numbers and original owners who had sold vehicles without transferring ownership to the new owners.

"Kajang Municipal Council does not bear any towing costs for abandoned vehicles, as it appoints the Car Medic panel to tow vehicles whose notice period has expired, in the presence of enforcement officers," he said.
He said abandoned vehicles also obstructed traffic and visibility, increasing the risk of accidents.
The spokesman said leaking oil and other fluids from abandoned vehicles could pollute soil and water, affect cleanliness and tarnish the area's image.
"The vehicles also have the potential to become breeding grounds for disease vectors and nesting places for pests, as well as depriving the public of parking bays," the spokesman said.
To address the problem, the council will appoint contractors to facilitate towing. It will also raise awareness among vehicle owners and publicise information on assistance with vehicle disposal.

6a1ac8b535070922: NEW YORK, Oct 13 — US photography company Getty Images announced Monday that it had reached an agreement with major lenders to restructure its debt, take the company private and undertake a “pre-packaged” bankruptcy.

Getty, which partners with AFP among numerous other media companies, said members of the Getty Family and affiliates of Koch Equity Development will invest up to US$533 million (RM2.25 billion) in new equity to pay down debt under the restructuring.
Getty “reached agreement with all of its major financial stakeholder groups on the terms of a comprehensive restructuring”, the company said.
Getty will continue to operate normally throughout the process, citing up to US$143 million (RM604.3 million) in financing from Koch, as well as cash from ongoing business.
“There is no anticipated impact on content contributors, partners, customers, or employees across the Company’s worldwide network,” Getty said.
The company plans a “prepackaged Chapter 11 filing” to win court approval of the restructuring.
“The requisite majority of creditors have committed to vote in favor of the Plan,” said Getty, which expects the restructuring to be complete by year’s end.

The announcement came after Getty disclosed in a securities filing earlier this month that it had been notified of plans to delist its shares from the New York Stock Exchange because they had fallen below US$1 (RM4.23).
Getty reported a loss of US$206.1 million (RM870 million) in 2025. — AFP
0385e485e32cca2d: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget reinforces Malaysia's commitment to strengthening its digital economy through investments in connectivity, artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and analysts say.

The initiatives aim to expand digital access, improve public services and boost economic competitiveness. However, analysts say effective implementation, domestic technology development and private sector participation will be crucial to achieving these goals.

Among the key initiatives are RM5 billion for the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA), RM1 billion for the national digital healthcare ecosystem and RM142 million to strengthen National Information Dissemination Centres (NADI).

The JENDELA allocation will expand high-quality Internet coverage in rural and remote areas, including Orang Asli villages. It will also improve connectivity along 7,000km of roads and highways, and 1,700km of rail routes nationwide.

The National Digital Healthcare Ecosystem and Connectivity Initiative (PERSADA) will improve digital infrastructure and connectivity in the healthcare sector. It will support the expansion of Electronic Medical Records, telehealth services and drone deliveries of medicines to improve access to healthcare in rural and remote areas.
The NADI allocation will strengthen its role as a digital community hub by providing training in digital skills and AI, while supporting local economic development and entrepreneurship.

The Madani Submarine Cable System (SALAM) will increase network capacity and resilience between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. WiFi at public higher education institutions and a Sovereign AI Cloud are also expected to improve connectivity and strengthen data sovereignty.

MCMC will intensify its Safe Internet Campaign in schools nationwide and continue efforts to combat digital fraud. These include blocking more than 5.7 billion scam-related calls and short message service messages.
MCMC said the initiatives would help ensure digital investments deliver tangible benefits to the people, industry and country.

Nusantara Academy for Strategic Research senior fellow Prof Azmi Hassan said the government's commitment was clearer when allocations across ministries and digital infrastructure projects were considered together, rather than focusing solely on the Digital Ministry's RM1.36 billion allocation.

"The government has shown its commitment through the combined allocations for ministries, education, infrastructure and AI to ensure Malaysia does not fall too far behind in the digital economy," he told Business Times.
Azmi welcomed the additional 100,000 free AI subscriptions, saying these could widen access to technology and improve young people's employability.
He said the RM142 million allocation for NADI could help small and medium enterprises explore new opportunities through its online business platform.
However, he said the initiatives' success should be measured by the number of jobs created and the foreign direct investment attracted to AI and other digital industries.

Institute of Strategic and International Studies Malaysia chairman Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Faiz Abdullah said the next challenge was ensuring businesses translated access to digital technology into productivity gains.

He said Malaysia needed to develop homegrown solutions that could compete internationally, with stronger support for domestically developed software and AI, start-ups, research and development, and talent development.
Faiz said AI adoption varied across sectors. Financial services were moving towards scaling up their strategies, while manufacturers remained largely at the experimentation stage.
Malaysia's ambition to establish 3,000 smart factories by 2030 remained a significant challenge, with only 93 having completed their transformation.

"Unless there is a massive acceleration in the build-up rate, this will set Malaysia back from the vision of realising dark factories which can function 24/7 without explicit human supervision," he said.
Faiz said Malaysia could build on its existing strengths in data centre construction, cooling systems and telecommunications, developing expertise that could be exported to other countries.
Other opportunities included advanced semiconductor packaging and AI applications in healthcare and agriculture.
He said connectivity investments would be more effective if rural communities had reliable electricity and fast Internet access.
He cited Sabah as an example of how energy constraints, slow Internet and limited economic opportunities could hinder digital transformation.
Faiz proposed state-by-state assessments of innovation, research and development, productivity and exports to identify bottlenecks and ensure digital initiatives addressed local needs.

National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) chief executive Dr Megat Zuhairy Megat Tajuddin said the 2027 vsupported efforts to strengthen Malaysia's technological sovereignty and prepare critical systems for emerging cyber threats.

"Ultimately, resilience requires more than adopting technologies developed elsewhere. We must harness our domestic talents, researchers and industry players to develop, test and deploy solutions that address national security needs," he said.
He said the collaboration between NACSA and MCMC would support the development of home-grown data protection technologies against quantum threats, alongside efforts to strengthen CSCDC Bhd.
Malaysia's National Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Plan 2025–2030 and AI Systems Cyber Security Framework would help prepare critical systems for emerging risks.

Megat Zuhairy said cybersecurity progress should be measured through stronger protection of critical infrastructure and personal information, faster incident responses and more reliable digital services.

An AI-powered scam-checking application could prevent financial losses, he said. However, it would need to be backed by intelligence-sharing, coordinated investigations and cross-border enforcement cooperation.

International Islamic University Malaysia professor of Asean studies and political science Dr Phar Kim Beng said Malaysia's digital transformation required effective execution and greater private-sector participation, given its limited fiscal room.
"Malaysia has a small budget to make any digital quantum leap," he said, stressing the need for public-private partnerships and safeguards against corruption and leakages.
Phar said Malaysia should strengthen its position in regional submarine cable infrastructure, with Selangor potentially becoming a hub supported by bunkering services for cable-laying vessels.
He called for stronger regional cooperation involving China, Japan, South Korea and Asean nations to combat cross-border online scams.

8b3c9f9cfafab653: SEREMBAN, Oct 13 — This isn’t mum’s cooking. More like... grandma’s cooking?
Fine, gossamer strands of thin rice vermicelli swimming in a dark braised gravy that is more soupy than saucy.
Chunks of pork, some lean, some fat. Then the sudden pop of a cephalopod tentacle.
This is a plate of squid bee hoon, as old school as you get. As close to grandma’s cooking as you’re likely to get outside your home. Or, to be specific here, Coffee Tiam Foo’s Cooking.
Located along the always bustling Jalan Temiang in Seremban, Coffee Tiam Foo’s Cooking is an institution in the old town area.
Certainly the place is packed and parking can be a challenge, but neither has deterred hungry customers, naturally.
The shop is open past lunchtime but most of the crowd is here for breakfast (which in Seremban often comes as a substantial bowl or plate of noodles).
Though one never starts with noodles, not immediately. One must appreciate proper protocol: kopi first, please. Caffeine before carbs.
Coffee here is still made the traditional way, with long-spouted coffee pots and flannel filters. The result is a strong brew, rich and intense. More bitter than sweet, to properly wake us up.
We enjoy our cups of kopi kaw with the requisite orders of half boiled eggs and butter kaya toast.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
‘Kopi’ and half boiled eggs.— Picture by CK Lim
The latter looks joyfully retro with its slightly irregular, rectangular shape, perfect for dipping into the eggs as thick soldiers.

Still, noodles are the main attraction here at Coffee Tiam Foo. Besides the squid bee hoon, other favourites include their Hakka mee (a Seremban staple), pork noodles, laksa, claypot loh shu fun and loh mee.
The last two also make an appearance, sort of, in a third dish that the proprietor recommended to us: Ah Yee loh shu fun.
Here the noodles of choice are the Hakka “silver needles” or loh shu fun (thinner and longer than the loh shu fun we are used to back in the Klang Valley).
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Butter ‘kaya’ toast. — Picture by CK Lim
But instead of a dark, caramelised claypot sauce, we have a thick, gelatinous gravy reminiscent of a loh mee, albeit clearer in colour.
Topped with minced pork, fried shallots and ribbons of Chinese style omelette, this is a hearty dish meant to keep one’s belly full for a full day of work ahead.
To go with our noodles, we shared some yong tau foo (another signature menu item of Coffee Tiam Foo), both the fried and soup versions.

There are over a dozen types of yong tau foo available, from fried sui kow and bean curd puffs to bitter gourd and eggplant filled with pork and fish meat. Homemade meatballs, crispy pork skin, fried tofu, stuffed chillies, and more.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Ah Yee ‘loh shu fun’. — Picture by CK Lim
All of it fantastic, though our favourite is their fish skin wrapped fish cake. One of the fried varieties, the crunch of the fish skin makes it so addictive... one piece won’t be enough.
Nor indeed, for some, just one plate of noodles.
For the flavours remain nostalgic, evoking that longing for home cooking at grandma’s house. Where else would one pair fresh, springy squid with luscious pork belly and a dark, heady gravy?

Fantastic ‘yong tau foo’, including a fish skin wrapped fish cake. — Picture by CK Lim

3a332e39eafcf626: PETALING JAYA: Kerajaan disaran mempertimbangkan persekolahan terus diadakan secara fizikal dengan memakai pelitup muka dalam kelas memandangkan kurang daripada 30% murid sekolah rendah di Johor mengikuti pengajaran dan pembelajaran di rumah (PdPR) ketika sekolah ditutup akibat jerebu.

Pengerusi Persatuan Penglibatan Ibu Bapa dan Komuniti Swasta Johor, Yahya Jaafar, berkata kadar penyertaan itu rendah berbanding kira-kira 70% pelajar sekolah menengah, yang dipercayai berpunca daripada kekangan ibu bapa bekerja, kekurangan peranti dan tiada bimbingan di rumah sehingga boleh menjejaskan kelancaran pembelajaran murid.

"Ketika pandemik Covid-19, ibu bapa kebanyakannya berada di rumah untuk membim­bing anak-anak mengikuti PdPR. Namun, keadaan kini berbeza ke­rana ramai ibu bapa bekerja dan tidak dapat memantau pem­belajaran anak-anak secara langsung," katanya menurut Utusan Malaysia.
Beliau turut menyarankan pergerakan murid dihadkan, khasnya di kawasan terbuka bagi mengurangkan pendedahan murid kepada udara tercemar.
"Bagi sekolah berasrama pula, pengajaran dan pembelajaran boleh dilaksana dalam asrama dengan guru turun membimbing murid, sekali gus mengawal pergerakan mereka."

Langkah lain, katanya, termasuk kerajaan dan majikan memberi kelonggaran cuti kepada ibu bapa, dengan menggunakan cuti tahunan atau bencana jika bersesuaian, bagi membolehkan mereka membimbing anak mengikuti PdPR.
Tegasnya, langkah itu penting kerana murid sekolah rendah masih memerlukan pemantauan rapi, selain memastikan proses pembelajaran tidak terjejas terlalu lama."
2b91094bc9adfeae: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 13 — A seven-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by a pack of six to eight stray dogs while playing at a playground near a low-cost housing flat in Lima Kedai here yesterday.

Kota Iskandar assemblyman Datuk Pandak Ahmad said the incident occurred between 3 pm and 4 pm, when the boy was believed to have been playing before the stray dogs attacked him, causing him to fall and roll on the ground as he tried to escape.
“Fortunately, a man who witnessed the incident threw stones at the dogs from a distance, helping to save the boy.
“I was informed of the incident by the village head and went to the flats to inspect the location,” he told Bernama when contacted.
He said the victim sustained injuries to the eye area, neck, head and body and was rushed to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for treatment.
Pandak said such incidents are deeply concerning and require immediate action by the authorities.
He said the incident was not the first of its kind in the area, as a 15-year-old boy had also been attacked by a pack of eight stray dogs at about 6 am the same day.
The teenager managed to drive the animals away before fleeing to the building’s staircase, but sustained injuries to his leg.
Pandak said he had met the teenager and advised him to seek treatment at a nearby clinic, while the seven-year-old boy is receiving treatment at HSA.

He said the matter had been brought to the attention of the local authority and he was informed that the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) would conduct an operation tonight to address the stray dog problem in the area.
He said appropriate action needs to be taken immediately to ensure the residents’ safety, particularly that of children, even if it might draw objections from non-governmental organisations (NGOs).
“How long are we going to allow this to happen? Do we have to wait for someone to die before action is taken?” he said.
He also visited the victim and expressed hope that effective measures would be implemented to prevent similar incidents, particularly in residential areas with public facilities for residents.

In an earlier incident on Sept 5, a two-year-old girl, Nur Haira Wafiqah, was reported to have sustained serious injuries after being attacked by five stray dogs in Kampung Tambak, Peserai, Batu Pahat.
The victim suffered serious injuries to several parts of her body in the attack. — Bernama
63968097b0942455: NEW YORK, Oct 13 — Oil prices rose on Monday as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi movement launched additional strikes on Saudi Arabia, adding to worries about tight global supplies heading into the northern hemisphere winter.
Several powerful explosions rattled the Saudi capital Riyadh on Monday night following a series of Houthi attacks at Riyadh airport in recent days that have killed at least 18 people.
Oil prices rose about 2 per cent, while global equity markets turned in a mixed performance as investors looked ahead to major US corporate earnings and economic data later in the week.
“We’re waiting for a lot of elements,” CFRA Research’s Sam Stovall said near the end of Monday’s session, which saw the Dow climb and the Nasdaq retreat.

“Investors are sort of holding their breath waiting for confirmation that the market was justified in setting a new all-time high on the S&P 500,” Stovall said, adding that this week’s inflation data was a particularly important source of interest.
An unexpectedly high inflation reading could increase the likelihood of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in October, Stovall said.
Saudi Arabia’s energy minister acknowledged that the kingdom’s infrastructure and resilience had been tested in the aftermath of the latest attacks.

“Energy security can’t be taken for granted,” Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a high-profile conference in Riyadh. “The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

Doubts surrounding US President Donald Trump’s claim of an “energy ceasefire” between Ukraine and Russia, following his surprise announcement of a deal to buy diesel from Moscow, further unsettled investors.

“Oil remains well bid above US$100 (RM423) after strikes on Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh airport over the weekend, while efforts to secure a Russia-Ukraine energy truce were muddy,” said Neil Wilson, a strategist at Saxo UK.

Russia on Monday refused to say whether an agreement had been reached with Ukraine to halt attacks on energy infrastructure, a day after Trump sowed confusion with his unilateral announcement of an “energy ceasefire”.
“It is increasingly evident that Russia is unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire proposed by the United States,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on social media.
“Today alone, the Russians have attacked six energy facilities in Ukraine. Thirty-three people were wounded across the country,” he added.
Also in focus this week is the start of the corporate earnings season, with US banking giants JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America due to report on Tuesday.
Technology giants will follow later in October and November, with traders keen to assess the outlook for the AI sector as it invests vast sums despite growing concerns over the technology.

Markets are bullish on company results overall, with companies in the S&P 500 expected to report a 24.3 per cent jump in earnings per share compared with the third quarter of 2025, according to CFRA. — AFP
