3ad908923ba319c6: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department conducted 12,343 operations against businesses illegally run by foreigners from 2024 to Sept 30 this year, resulting in the detention of 25,124 foreigners, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.

He said the operations comprised Op Belanja, targeting business and retail premises; Op Jaja, focusing on hawker activities; and Op Selera, targeting restaurants, eateries and food preparation premises.
He said 5,173 operations were conducted under Op Belanja, involving inspections of 20,882 people, with a total of 5,809 undocumented migrants and 471 employers detained.
For Op Jaja, 567 operations were carried out, involving inspections of 8,473 people. These resulted in the detention of 734 undocumented migrants and 40 employers.
Meanwhile, 6,603 Op Selera operations were conducted, involving inspections of 51,847 people. A total of 19,301 undocumented migrants and 1,341 employers were detained.
Saifuddin said action was taken under the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Immigration Regulations 1963 against foreigners found staying or working illegally in the country.
"Common offences included not possessing a valid pass or permit, overstaying and violating the conditions of a pass or permit.

"Those convicted could face fines or imprisonment. Foreigners ordered to be deported would be placed at immigration depots while documentation and travel documents were arranged with their respective embassies or diplomatic representatives before being sent home," he said in a parliamentary written reply.

On allegations that syndicates or other parties were protecting illegal business activities, Saifuddin said all information and complaints received would be examined through intelligence gathering and further investigations.
He said the department would continue intelligence-led and targeted enforcement operations through Op Belanja, Op Jaja and Op Selera to curb the abuse of immigration facilities by foreigners.
67f0eda8e128dac5: WASHINGTON: US federal agents searched the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar on Monday as part of what officials said was a criminal investigation, marking a dramatic escalation in President Donald Trump's confrontation with the outspoken lawmaker.
Omar said she was "ok" following the operation but accused the administration of targeting political opponents just three weeks before she seeks re-election in the Nov 3 midterms.

The early morning search – described by Trump's "border czar" Tom Homan as part of a longstanding probe – was conducted by agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of US immigration enforcement.
"Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponise federal law enforcement," Omar wrote on X.
"For 10 years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation."
The operation also sparked a furious backlash from Democrats who accused Trump of abusing government powers to pursue his political opponents.

Fox News reported that the search was linked to a criminal fraud investigation concerning immigration paperwork submitted on behalf of the Somali-born congresswoman by her late father when she was a child.
The president was asked about Omar hours after the operation and said she was being investigated "very carefully."

"I've always found her to be totally crooked personally, but that has nothing to do with me. I think she's a terrible person, just a complainer. She comes from a country that is a non-country," he told reporters at the White House.

The Justice Department confirmed in a statement Monday that agents had carried out a "judicially authorised search warrant" in the Washington area, but officials did not identify Omar or disclose the nature of the probe.
"This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation," prosecutors added.
Omar, 44, is a leftist Democrat and fierce critic of Trump, particularly his administration's sweeping crackdown on immigration.
The Republican president has repeatedly clashed with Omar, who came to the United States from Somalia as a child and has frequently been the target of his political attacks.

Top House Democrat Hakeem Jeffries and his leadership team called the search "deeply disturbing" and raised questions about "the continued corrupt weaponisation of the federal government against Donald Trump's adversaries."
Minnesota's Democratic Governor Tim Walz accused Trump of "abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."
Republican congresswoman Nancy Mace, meanwhile, said Omar should be stripped of her US citizenship and deported if fraud was proven.
"NO ONE is above the law," she wrote on X.
The timing also drew criticism from Xochitl Hinojosa, a former director of public affairs at the Justice Department.
"There's a longstanding rule at DOJ that you don't take overt actions like this before an election, especially when there's a candidate on the ballot," she wrote on X.
Omar said in September that Homeland Security officials had not contacted her about any investigation, dismissing the allegations against her as politically motivated attacks.
Omar was first elected to Congress in 2018 and represents a district including Minneapolis, home to one of the largest Somali communities in the United States.
She is a member of the group of left-wing Democratic lawmakers known as "The Squad," who have been among Trump's most vocal opponents in Congress.
No charges against Omar were announced in connection with Monday's search.

8aa88869e63eef3e: MIAMI: A jersey worn by basketball legend Michael Jordan during the 1998 NBA Finals has sold for US$14 million, setting what auction house Hunt Auctions described as a record for basketball memorabilia, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls’ red jersey during Game 2 of the Finals against the Utah Jazz, helping his team secure a victory that tied the series at 1-1. The Bulls went on to win the series in six games, securing Jordan’s sixth and final NBA championship.
Hunt Auctions said the jersey was purchased in a private sale by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman, according to The Guardian.

“Michael Jordan’s importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established,” said Hunt Auctions President David Hunt, adding that the market had developed into an “elite asset class” comparable with iconic works of art.
The US$14 million sale is the second-highest known price paid for a game-worn jersey, behind the US$24.12 million paid in 2024 for a Babe Ruth jersey worn during the 1932 World Series.

Jordan memorabilia from the 1998 Finals has drawn particularly strong demand. A jersey he wore in Game 1 sold for about US$10.1 million in 2022, while another worn during Game 3 fetched about US$12.3 million at auction last month.
The 1997–98 season was chronicled in the documentary series The Last Dance, which became a global hit following its release on Netflix in 2020.
2239720304052e19: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Social media influencers have been reminded not to exploit issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R), particularly religious rituals, for online content, in the interest of preserving harmony in the country’s multiracial society.
Deputy National Unity Minister R. Yuneswaran said influencers with large followings should be more responsible in producing content and spreading positive values instead of playing on 3R sentiments.
"If possible, stay away from issues involving 3R, as influencers may not know about the religious rituals or customs of certain communities, especially if they do not profess that religion.
"We have many positive things that can be promoted together with the National Unity Ministry,” he said when met after attending Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme at Wisma Bernama yesterday.
He was commenting on a viral issue involving an influencer believed to have participated in a religious ceremony during the Thaipusam celebration at Batu Caves, Selangor.

Yuneswaran said the ministry viewed the issue involving religious rituals seriously and hoped it would be handled tactfully, adding that the investigation had been left entirely to the religious authorities and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
He also urged the public not to rush to judgement or politicise the issue, but to allow the authorities to conduct their investigation and resolve the matter promptly.
In addition, he invited social media influencers to work with the ministry to promote the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and the National Nationhood Programme.

"Under the ministry, we recommend that these issues (3R) be avoided. Although our society comprises people of various races and ethnic groups, we can attend various ceremonies, events and celebrations; however, when rituals are involved, I hope they will be respected,” he said.

On Sunday, the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) confirmed that it had begun investigating a viral post involving an individual believed to be Muslim who was alleged to have participated in another religion’s ritual in contravention of Islamic law. — Bernama
4bd33d436ac2b18d: AUBAGNE, Oct 13 — A 14-year-old boy opened fire with a hunting gun at a middle school in France on Monday, wounding the headmaster and a teacher before being disarmed by a member of staff, local authorities said.
The shooting took place at Joseph-Lakanal middle school in the southern town of Aubagne, near Marseille, where a third person was grazed by gunfire, police said.
Authorities said there did not appear to be a link to high school protests that have rocked France in recent weeks.
“The middle school was not affected by the high school students’ protest,” police told AFP.
The suspect “came in carrying a bag which was a guitar case. He clearly removed a weapon from this guitar case — a long gun,” said Marseille’s deputy public prosecutor Audrey Jouaneton.
He fired at least four shots, including inside a classroom occupied by teachers and pupils, leaving a mark on a blackboard, she added.
The headmaster, 53, and teacher, 37, were not in critical condition, according to authorities.

“The suspect, for reasons as yet unknown, fired at the headteacher, who was hit by a shower of pellets in the thighs and lower back,” said Jacques Witkowski, prefect of the wider Bouches-du-Rhône region.
He then fired at a second teacher, who was hit by buckshot in the thigh before a member of staff disarmed him, he said.
The suspect “is not known for any history of delinquency or radicalisation”, Witkowski added.
Sarah, a pupil at the school, told AFP she heard the fire alarm go off during her Spanish lesson and went into the corridor, where she and her classmates “bumped into” the gunman.
“He started shooting and said: ‘I’ve only come for the teachers, not for the pupils,’” she said.
An investigation into attempted murder has been opened.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who visited the scene, said the suspect’s parents had been taken into custody.
Investigators were “trying to understand how this young person ended up in a position with this gun”, Nunez told reporters.
‘Prevent the worst’
French President Emmanuel Macron praised the teaching staff for their quick reaction in a post on X.
“I commend the composure and exemplary response of the teaching staff, which helped to prevent the worst from happening,” he said.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray, who also visited the scene on Monday, called for action against such violence.
“All this seems to sit within a global social phenomenon,” he said. “We have to provide a societal response... Schools can’t do everything, schools cannot treat major violence.”
There has been a spate of violent incidents at French schools in recent months, prompting bag checks on entry at some establishments.
In February, a 14-year-old stabbed an art teacher in southern France at least three times, leaving the 60-year-old in critical condition.
A 14-year-old student in June last year fatally stabbed a teaching assistant in eastern France.
In another incident, a student carried out a stabbing spree in several classrooms in April last year, wounding a girl and three other pupils. — AFP
2716a3eb65547a0f: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration is planning to move three senior officials from the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence (CAISSI) to the White House, news website The Information reported on Monday, citing a White House official.
The White House and commerce department could not be immediately reached for comment.

Commerce secretary Howard Lutnick invited two White House officials, Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross, to co-manage CAISSI six months ago, the report said, citing a senior Commerce Department official.
The three CAISSI officials, whose names have not been disclosed, will report to Kratsios and Cairncross, according to the report.

A White House official told The Information that coordination problems with the commerce department highlighted the need for CAISSI's leadership to be moved closer to the White House's AI decision-making process.
CAISSI, a commerce department unit that evaluates advanced AI models for safety and capabilities, plays a role in the administration's framework for testing frontier AI systems before deployment.

This month, Trump named National Intelligence director Jay Clayton the administration's AI czar, tasking him with coordinating the federal government's efforts to maintain US leadership in the technology.
9b920fee46561273: LOS ANGELES, Oct 13 — RJ Mitte, the young actor best known for playing Walter White Jr. in the award-winning TV series Breaking Bad, has died, his representatives told AFP on Monday. He was 34.
The cause of death for the actor, who lived with cerebral palsy, was not immediately revealed.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” said a statement issued by Sean Reilly.
A teenage Mitte first appeared in Breaking Bad in 2008 as the son of chemistry-teacher-turned-drug-kingpin Walter White, a role that won Bryan Cranston global acclaim.
“Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion,” Reilly said.
That campaigning evolved into working as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and for Shriners Children’s, a nonprofit hospital network.

“He also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, supporting philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities,” Reilly added.

Breaking Bad, which ran for five seasons between 2008 and 2013, is routinely acclaimed as groundbreaking television, and was recently named by The New York Times as the best TV show of the 21st century.
Co-stars rushed to pay tribute to the performer, with Aaron Paul — who played Jesse Pinkman, White’s young partner in crime — saying he was “at a loss” over the news.
“RJ, I love you my friend. You will be missed,” he said, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
“And to whoever happens to be reading this, please know you are loved, and you are not alone. Always remember that.”
Dean Norris, who starred in the series as Mitte’s on-screen uncle, a special agent with the Drug Enforcement Agency, said he was “heartbroken” by the news of the young man’s death.
“Though RJ didn’t play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set,” Norris wrote on social media.
“He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed. This is so heartbreaking, I can’t believe it. Thinking of him and his family.”

Fellow actor and disability campaigner Marlee Matlin, who appeared with Mitte in Cinemability: The Art of Inclusion, a documentary that examined the history of disability portrayals in US film and television, said her heart was “shattered.”

“There will never be another like RJ Mitte. You will always have a place in my heart. RIP,” wrote Matlin, who became the first deaf actress to win an Oscar when she scooped the top honour for Children of a Lesser God. — AFP
bfa0fbe568cbc758: SYDNEY: Australian business conditions were broadly unchanged in September, though confidence slipped further amid a surge in oil prices driven by renewed tensions in the Middle East, raising concerns over higher costs, a survey showed on Tuesday.

The survey from National Australia Bank showed its index of business conditions was flat at -1 in September. However, the ongoing decline in confidence suggests that conditions will likely deteriorate further, the survey said.
Confidence fell 4 points to -13, well below the level recorded in February, before the US-Israeli conflict with Iran began.
"Energy prices remain elevated, funding costs have risen and domestic growth has slowed in 2026," NAB said.
"Against this backdrop, it is not surprising that both business confidence and business conditions are well below their respective long-run averages."

Over the month, business confidence fell in five out of eight industries. Mining, wholesale and retail saw "some improvement" in sentiment, though in trend terms, confidence remains negative across all industries except mining, NAB said.

Global oil prices experienced extreme volatility in September after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis launched missile and drone strikes against Saudi Arabia. The conflict, now a spillover of the broader US-Iran tensions, has driven oil prices higher, fuelling fears of persistent inflation.
The Reserve Bank of Australia last month raised its cash rate to a 15-year high of 4.60 per cent - its fourth hike of the year - and warned it may have to tighten further to curb inflation.
623e5efabfb9d9e0: PETALING JAYA: The Bar Council has introduced a new rule requiring two partners in a legal firm to act as signatories for cheques, and to manage the multi-factor authentication for online transactions involving clients' accounts.

The Bar said the rule, which will take effect next year, was introduced following concerns over “significant” high insurance payouts arising from misconduct and dishonesty in managing clients' accounts.

“This trend is unsustainable, as substantial payouts will inevitably result in higher overall losses and, over time, increased premiums for all firms," the circular, which was issued on Sept 25, read.

The new rule requires legal firms with more than one partner to have two partners as signatories for all transactions, except for stopping account operations or cancelling transactions, where one will suffice.
Firms using electronic banking must also implement multi-factor authentication for access to clients' accounts, managed by the firm's partners.
While many firms already apply similar safeguards, the new rule seeks to standardise these practices without imposing unnecessary burdens, the circular read.
537e47971806fa23: KUALA LUMPUR: Preparing a cup of coffee might seem simple, but for Sky Soong, it takes patience, practice and, occasionally, a helping hand.
The 44-year-old, who is vision impaired, sometimes struggles to locate ingredients, handle equipment or notice when something has fallen.
But these are challenges he is gradually learning to work around at Blind Brew, a drinks stall in Brickfields he has been running for the past two months.
“It is difficult to run a stall because our vision is blurry. Sometimes things fall or are hard to find, and we may need to ask others for help,” he told FMT Lifestyle.
Originally from Kota Bharu, Kelantan, Soong began experiencing blurred vision at 17. His eyesight gradually deteriorated, although he never knew why.
The change brought uncertainty, particularly about his future and his chances of finding work.
“There are not many jobs available for blind people. Twenty years ago, even going to college was difficult because computers were not suitable for us,” he shared.

Determined to become more self-reliant, Soong enrolled at the Malaysian Association for the Blind’s Gurney Training Centre, where he learnt practical skills such as using a white cane, cooking and navigating daily life.
Just as importantly, he discovered a community. “I learnt how blind people live and realised there are others like me. Some are partially blind, while others are completely blind,” he said.
It was also where he befriended Foo Yi Xeng, who would become one of Blind Brew’s co-founders.
Soong went on to work as a freelance massage therapist for more than 20 years before deciding to try something different.
Blind Brew was established with support from Kuala Lumpur-based NGO Persatuan Amal Indah, which provided about RM5,000 to help get the stall started.
The menu includes coffee, soya bean drinks, mango and peach jasmine green teas, cendol and Chinese tea eggs.
For Soong, the stall is about more than earning an income. “I want to help more people understand how blind people live. Empathy is more important than pity,” he said.
Running the business has meant learning through repetition. Soong relies on familiarity to remember where ingredients are kept and to make each drink as consistently as possible.
“You need to keep practising and understand where everything is placed. After repeating the process many times, you become more familiar with it."
Mistakes still happen. Preparing cendol, for instance, has proved challenging, particularly when he needs to judge whether ingredients such as coconut milk are still fresh.
“When we make mistakes, we’re not happy about it. We just hope we won’t repeat them,” he said.
Thankfully, customers have generally been understanding, offering feedback rather than criticism.
And few things make Soong happier than hearing that his efforts are paying off.
“When customers tell us our offerings such as cendol are better than before, we feel very happy and appreciated. It shows that we’re improving,” he said.
Business may be unpredictable, but Soong has no intention of throwing in the towel. For him, improvement comes from turning up, practising and trying again.
“Every day, when you keep doing something, you improve,” he concluded.
Blind Brew 21, Jalan Tun Sambanthan 4 Brickfields, 50470 Kuala Lumpur

700d5d8c29370ba3: PETALING JAYA: Majlis Peguam memperkenalkan peraturan baharu yang mewajibkan dua rakan kongsi dalam firma guaman bertindak sebagai penandatangan cek serta mengurus pengesahan berbilang faktor bagi transaksi dalam talian yang melibatkan akaun anak guam.

“Trend ini tidak mampan kerana bayaran tuntutan yang besar pasti mengakibatkan peningkatan keseluruhan kerugian dan, dari semasa ke semasa, kenaikan premium bagi semua firma,” menurut pekeliling yang dikeluarkan pada 25 Sept.

Peraturan baharu itu mewajibkan firma guaman yang mempunyai lebih daripada seorang rakan kongsi melantik dua rakan kongsi sebagai penandatangan bagi semua urus niaga, kecuali untuk menghentikan operasi akaun atau membatalkan urus niaga, yang memadai dilakukan oleh seorang sahaja.
Firma yang menggunakan perbankan elektronik juga mesti melaksanakan pengesahan berbilang faktor untuk mengakses akaun anak guam, yang diuruskan oleh rakan kongsi firma berkenaan.

Walaupun banyak firma sudah melaksanakan langkah perlindungan yang serupa, pekeliling itu menyatakan bahawa peraturan baharu berkenaan bertujuan menyeragamkan amalan tersebut tanpa mengenakan beban yang tidak perlu.
e949d027e99604f1: PETALING JAYA: Less than 30% of primary school pupils in Johor have been taking part in online learning following the temporary closure of schools due to the haze, says a parents' group.

Yahya Jaafar, chairman of Persatuan Penglibatan Ibu Bapa dan Komuniti Swasta Negeri Johor, said this was in stark contrast with the 70% of secondary school students who have been following online lessons.
Yahya attributed the low figure for primary school pupils to limitations faced by working parents and a lack of devices and guidance at home, Utusan Malaysia reported.
He expressed concern that this could affect students' learning if the haze persists, especially those sitting for their Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia examination this year.
"During the Covid-19 pandemic, parents were mostly at home, so they could help their children follow the online lessons.
"The situation is different now because many parents are still working and aren't able to directly monitor their children," he said.
Yahya suggested that schools reopen with everyone mandated to wear masks while in class. He said students could also be restricted from open spaces to reduce exposure to the haze.
"For boarding schools, lessons could be held in the dorms," he said.

Schools in Johor remain closed today due to the haze. As of 8am, the air pollutant index reading in Pasir Gudang stood at 180, followed by Larkin (176), Kota Tinggi (169), Pengerang (166), Batu Pahat (161), Kluang (154), Tangkak (151) and Segamat (133).

Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said yesterday that schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan and Putrajaya would be closed today due to the haze.
An API reading of zero to 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy and above 300 as hazardous.
6690c7007010fe87: KOTA BARU: The female teacher who struck two Form One students, killing one of them, in front of the surau at SMK Tanjong Mas in April arrived at the Kota Baru courts complex.
The 57-year-old faces two charges under Section 304A of the Penal Code for causing death by negligence and Section 336 of the same Act for endangering life or personal safety.
It was reported that a Form One girl was killed while another was seriously injured after being struck by a vehicle driven by the teacher in front of the school surau on April 12.
d80d8068281ae623: SANAA, Oct 13 — A Houthi official on Monday warned the US it would receive a “painful response” if it entered the war in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested Washington’s help in dealing with the group as it weathers repeated attacks.

Yemen’s civil war – in which a Saudi-led military coalition supports the government against the Iran-backed Houthis – reignited in July, months into the wider regional conflict that has roiled energy markets and plunged the Middle East into crisis.
The Houthis quickly began targeting Saudi oil facilities, tankers and transport hubs, including a string of lethal strikes on Riyadh’s airport, rocking the world’s top oil exporter.
Blasts resounded over the capital again on Monday night, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile and the group saying it had again targeted the airport.
Later, the coalition announced that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles in the south of the kingdom, near the border with Yemen.

In a statement posted on X, the coalition said it had “intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Khamis Mushait”, a city where a Saudi military base has previously come under attack.

Following an attack at Riyadh airport on Saturday that killed 13 people, US President Donald Trump said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the group, after reportedly rebuffing previous requests for help from the kingdom.
“The Houthis are misbehaving very badly. They’re misbehaving very badly. No good,” Trump said on Monday.

“If the US becomes involved in the aggression against Yemen, we will not deliberate over the decision to respond, rather, there will be a swift and painful response targeting the US and all its interests in the region,” Houthi political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti told AFP in an interview.
He also warned “all employees and workers at Saudi oil facilities and airports to stay away from these sites, as they have become legitimate targets”.
Saturday’s strike on King Khalid International Airport was the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade, and also left hundreds wounded.

Trump said the attack was “not acceptable” and that he would be speaking to the kingdom’s de facto leader, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, telling reporters the US was “going to look at” the possibility of joining Saudi strikes.
Operations remained suspended at the sprawling airport on Riyadh’s outskirts on Monday.
‘Serious’ response
Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman told a conference in Riyadh on Monday that the recent events had “tested our infrastructure, our institutions, our people, and our resilience”.
“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious.”

CCTV footage of Saturday’s attack released by Saudi authorities showed Muslim pilgrims in religious attire waiting in departure lounges before a sudden blast tore through the building and brought down flaming debris.
The atmosphere in Riyadh remained tense on Monday, as state broadcaster Al Ekhbariya said the military coalition was responding to drone and missile threats.
In the evening, mobile phones received a loud government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat” before the announcement of the interception.
The alert delayed the kickoff of a football match between Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana and Saudi team Al Nassr, home to Portuguese superstar Cristiano Ronaldo.
It was the first use of the phone alert system in Riyadh in weeks, with no official reason given for the lack of messaging during attacks targeting the capital in recent days.
The Houthis said they had also targeted the Khamis Mushait base in the kingdom’s south with a drone.
Flights suspended

The US embassy in Saudi Arabia said US government employees must obtain its authorisation before using any airport in the kingdom, and urged US citizens to “take extreme caution” if they chose to do so.
The mission also said “American citizens have been detained for taking photos of recent events” in Saudi Arabia.
The UAE’s national carrier Etihad Airways announced on Monday that it was cancelling all flights to and from Riyadh until next week, and had also suspended flights to Dammam and Jeddah.
Bahrain’s national carrier Gulf Air said it too was cancelling all Riyadh flights until Saturday.
US operator Delta announced it would delay the launch of direct flights from Atlanta to Riyadh, scheduled for October 23.
Despite vast spending on military hardware, Houthi attacks on oil, military and transport facilities across the large, mostly desert country are stretching Saudi defences.
Thomas Juneau, a security analyst at the University of Ottawa, said that despite some success, “Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves”.

Riyadh leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa.
Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.
The long-running Yemeni civil war has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.

UN rights chief Volker Turk said he was “appalled by the repeated attacks” on Saudi Arabia, but urged both sides to back down, adding that “continued fighting will only unleash further misery with no end in sight”. — AFP
13f7fe50340df958: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit edged higher against the US dollar at the opening, buoyed by optimism surrounding Budget 2027.
At 8am, the ringgit was up marginally against the greenback to 4.0815/4.0900 from Monday’s close of 4.0820/4.0865.

Nevertheless, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said heightened geopolitical risk in the Middle East and the anticipation of higher US inflation are expected to support the US dollar.

He said the situation in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following the missile attacks suggested that the current situation could potentially morph into a wider conflict, leading to further disruption to crude oil supplies.

“Brent crude oil prices have already risen by 1.38% to US$106.16 per barrel. Thus far, the US Dollar Index (DXY) has risen by 0.35% to 102.573 points, while the US Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation rate, to be released on Wednesday, is expected to increase to 3.6% in September (August: 3.4%), based on consensus estimates.
“On that note, the ringgit will likely continue trading within a narrow range,” Afzanizam said.
At the opening, the ringgit traded mostly firmer against a basket of major and Asean currencies.

The local note fell against the Japanese yen to 2.5748/2.5803 from 2.5739/2.5769 at Monday’s close, climbed against the British pound to 5.3913/5.4025 from 5.4017/5.4077, and strengthened against the euro to 4.5545/4.5640 from 4.5637/4.5687 at Monday’s close.

Against its Asean peers, the local note edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.8/228.4 from 227.9/228.2, but was almost flat against the Philippine peso at 6.50/6.52 compared with 6.50/6.51 at Monday’s close.
The ringgit edged up against the Singapore dollar to 3.1864/3.1933 from 3.1873/3.1911 at Monday’s close and strengthened against the Thai baht to 12.1318/12.1628 from 12.1391/12.1568.
ec8a6a705e418d7a: WASHINGTON, Oct 13 — US House Speaker Mike Johnson said he had reservations about a planned livestreamed execution in an interview broadcast by CBS News on Monday.
Nidal Hasan, 56, was sentenced to be executed by firing squad on December 3 at Fort Hood, Texas, where he shot and killed 13 people in 2009.

The decision to livestream the execution – which would be the first US military execution by firing squad since 1945 – has drawn widespread criticism, with the top congressional Republican adding his voice to the debate.

“The concern would be that you would create a video that would be a recruiting tool for future terrorists,” Johnson told CBS News, adding: “We’ve got to think through the policy implications of all that.”
The Republican lawmaker said he would not watch the execution if it were broadcast live.
“There are colleagues who have concerns,” he said.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth defended the idea of livestreaming the execution, saying: “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public.”
President Donald Trump, for his part, has said a final decision on whether the execution would be broadcast live remains to be made. — AFP
da232ca750a7afaf: MERCEDES driver George Russell could take another engine penalty at next month's Las Vegas Grand Prix, by which time teammate Kimi Antonelli is likely to have clinched the Formula One championship.

Russell, second in the standings but 102 points behind the Italian with six rounds remaining, started at the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix after exceeding his season's allocation of power units.
He said last week that he would be taking another penalty before the end of the season.
"It'll probably be later in the season now, to be honest. Maybe looking at Vegas," he told Sky Sports television after finishing ninth at Marina Bay.
"Now we've got the choice to take it when we wish, and we'll be choosing a slightly easier track than this one."

Russell and Mercedes had not planned to take a new engine in Singapore, a circuit where it is hard to overtake, but their hands were forced by a failure that sidelined the Briton at the previous Bahrain round in Malaysia and gave them no choice.
Austin, Texas would have been the preferred choice option on October 25.
Antonelli, 20, has his first chance to become the sport's youngest ever champion in Austin.

The winner of eight grands prix this year will have to win there, however, to become Italy's first champion since 1953 with five rounds to spare – and it will still depend on Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton not scoring enough to remain in contention.
Mexico a week later, or Brazil the weekend after, look more likely venues to witness the championship success before Las Vegas.
There can be no doubt that Antonelli will prevail eventually, with third-placed Hamilton now 111 points adrift and only 125 available after Austin.
If Antonelli wins in Texas then Red Bull's Max Verstappen, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's reigning champion Lando Norris will be out of title contention immediately.
Four-times champion Verstappen, winner on Sunday, will be chasing his third successive victory in the next race. — REUTERS
e13624479e566951: TOKYO: Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8 per cent in the year to September as companies passed on fuel and chemical costs, according to data released on Tuesday, highlighting mounting inflationary pressure that keeps alive market expectations of a near-term interest rate hike.
The data will be among the factors that the Bank of Japan will scrutinise when its board produces fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts at this month's policy meeting.

The rise in the corporate goods price index, which measures the price companies charge each other for their goods and services, compared with the median market forecast for a 7.6 per cent increase. It followed a 7.6 per cent gain in August.

The yen-based import price index surged 24.5 per cent in September from a year earlier, the data released by the BOJ showed, a sign that the currency's weakness continued to push up the cost of raw material imports.
2a4d1719289748ee: SYDNEY, Oct 13 — A Melbourne imam whose Islamic community centre has been linked by prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates to the co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a flydubai jet has said he “never met” the man and insisted he has “consistently preached peace”.

The Omani co-pilot, now in custody in the UAE, had drawn inspiration from Al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 suicide attacks and carried out his attempt “with the aim of causing the greatest possible loss of life”, according to the Emirati prosecutor’s findings published by state media last week.

The prosecutor said the co-pilot was first radicalised while studying in Australia “through reading extremist literature and following online content glorifying terrorist organisations and suicide attacks”.
The prosecutor alleged he was acquainted there with an organisation known as “My Centre”, managed by a Lebanese man called Abu Hamza.
Neither “My Centre” nor Abu Hamza has been accused of any criminal wrongdoing.
In a statement posted on social media late on Monday, Abu Hamza – also named by local media as Samir Mohtadi – said he had “never met” the co-pilot identified in reports as Hamam al-Hammami.
“We have no record of him ever attending our centre,” he said.
“The relevant authorities should have verified these claims with me before releasing or publishing such information,” he added.
He said he had “consistently preached peace” throughout his life.
“We unequivocally reject violence in all its forms.”
Police and intelligence services in Australia have said they are investigating the co-pilot’s links to the country.
Police in New Zealand said last week that he had spent time in the country on a six-month student visa, where he completed part of his flight training, national broadcaster RNZ reported. — AFP
451b8741daddeed7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — The implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage next June is structured to provide businesses and corporations with an adequate transition window to adjust their salary frameworks, Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said.

Speaking to reporters following the Post-Budget 2027 Debate organised by the Malaysian Economic Association in Kuala Lumpur yesterday, Johan identified sluggish wage growth relative to living expenses as the primary driver of household financial strain, even as headline inflation remains contained.
“This is why driving up the people's earning power is so critical. Raising the minimum wage is part of that strategy.
“While it isn't a silver bullet on its own, it plays a vital role and we are starting with large companies,” Johan said.

Johan said that the broader policy goal extends beyond lifting wages for entry-level workers to preventing wage compression, an outcome where pay raises for the lowest tier inadvertently squeeze differentials while intermediate salaries remain stagnant.
“The hope is that these large companies will also look at their overall salary structures and make adjustments based on the increase in the minimum wage.

“This is why the government mandated that government-linked-companies (GLC) adopt a living wage baseline of RM3,400, setting a benchmark for the private sector to follow when determining salary levels,” he said.

Johan noted that the RM2,000 baseline was deliberated and endorsed without contention by the National Wages Consultative Council, which comprises representatives from both trade unions and employer federations.
Extended adjustment window for small businesses

However, the Cabinet decided to grant an extended adjustment grace period for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to buffer them against operational cost shocks while they navigate the economic spillover effects of ongoing Middle East geopolitical tensions.

Alongside the RM2,000 statutory minimum wage and the RM3,400 GLC living wage threshold, Johan said the government will also maintain momentum on the Progressive Wage Policy, with plans also underway to introduce a dedicated minimum wage tier for semi-skilled occupations.
328abbcd508c47bd: KUALA LUMPUR: Datin Winnie Loo's five-year presidency of the Branding Association of Malaysia began during one of the most uncertain periods for businesses.

Taking the helm while the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted businesses and communities, Loo said the experience changed how she viewed leadership, branding and the association's role in the wider business ecosystem.
"The pandemic taught me that leadership is not about having all the answers. It is about staying calm, staying connected and giving people confidence when the future is uncertain," she said.
For Loo, the presidency became a period of transformation as the Branding Association of Malaysia evolved from an industry association into a platform connecting people, brands and communities.

Initiatives including the Brand Legend Awards, WOW Conference, Malaysia Brand Day, CEO Bootcamp series and BAM Ace the New Year were designed not merely as events, but as platforms for recognition, knowledge-sharing and relationship-building.

"What gives me the greatest satisfaction is knowing that the Branding Association of Malaysia became more visible, more inclusive and more relevant to the wider business community. That, to me, is a meaningful legacy," she said.
LEADING THROUGH UNCERTAINTY
Loo said the pandemic reinforced her belief that brands were ultimately built by people, with empathy and resilience becoming as important as strategy.
When businesses were struggling, so was her salon group, A Cut Above Group Sdn Bhd.
She said this made it important for the association to become a source of connection, encouragement and knowledge rather than simply an association that organised activities.
Her approach to leadership also evolved, with greater emphasis on consultation, collaboration and adapting to change.
BUILDING BEYOND BRANDING
Loo said businesses had increasingly recognised that branding extended beyond logos, advertising and visual identity to encompass people, purpose, reputation, digital presence and trust.
However, she said the industry still needed greater consistency and long-term thinking, as enduring brand equity could not be built through a single campaign or viral moment.
She also viewed the association's role as extending beyond its membership.
"Branding is connected to how Malaysia is perceived — our businesses, entrepreneurs, talent, culture and ability to compete internationally."
As the association's first female president in more than two decades, Loo said she hoped to create more opportunities for women leaders and entrepreneurs.
She urged her successor, Michelle Hah, to lead with purpose rather than position.
A NEW CHAPTER
Loo, 70, said stepping down did not mean retiring from purpose.
She plans to remain involved with the association as a mentor, adviser or speaker while focusing more on A Cut Above, writing, personal branding and mentoring the next generation of entrepreneurs.
"I may have stepped down from a title, but I have not stepped down from my purpose."

1d46bc53dd25941c: KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat is set to discuss the implementation of the RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027, the registration of Myanmar refugees, and measures to address the humanitarian crisis in Gaza today.

According to the Order Paper on Parliament's official portal, during the Minister's Question Time (MQT), Aminolhuda Hassan (PH-Sri Gading) will ask the economy minister to explain government mechanisms to ensure the minimum wage implementation does not result in job losses, price hikes, or increased operating costs for small enterprises.

Jimmy Puah Wee Tse (PH-Tebrau) will ask the home minister about the target for registering Myanmar refugees over the next two years through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) Programme, including targeted numbers and implementation timeline.

Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman (PN-Sik) will ask the foreign minister to outline the government's strategic steps following three years of genocide in Gaza, particularly in strengthening protection for Palestinians, humanitarian aid access, international accountability, and the reconstruction of Gaza.

During the question-and-answer session, Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Kubang Kerian) will ask the energy transition and water transformation minister about the expected new net generation capacity operating by 2030 and the capacity committed through Power Supply Agreements with data centres.

Ahmad Johnie Zawawi (GPS-Igan) will ask the education minister about the number of reserve teacher candidates among Sarawakians awaiting appointment, teaching vacancies according to options, and plans to absorb them.

Datuk Mohd Isam Mohd Isa (BN-Tampin) will ask the domestic trade and cost of living minister for an update on a study to enact specific legislation against ticket scalping, including existing legal loopholes that hinder enforcement.

Following the question-and-answer session, the house will continue debating the Supply Bill 2027 at the policy stage, following the tabling of Budget 2027 by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also finance minister, on Friday.

According to the calendar for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament, the policy-stage debate on Budget 2027 will run from Oct 12 to 22, followed by a four-day ministerial winding-up session starting Oct 26.
The Dewan Rakyat sits for 37 days until Dec 8. — BERNAMA
8e05284e42475dba: PETALING JAYA: Sebanyak 19 kawasan di seluruh negara mencatatkan bacaan Indeks Pencemaran Udara (IPU) tidak sihat pagi ini, dengan Sabah dan Sarawak sekali lagi terjejas akibat keadaan berjerebu.

Setakat 8 pagi, Pasir Gudang di Johor mencatatkan bacaan tertinggi dengan 180, manakala kawasan lain di negeri itu turut terjejas teruk, iaitu Larkin (176), Kota Tinggi (169), Pengerang (166), Batu Pahat (161), Kluang (154), Tangkak (151) dan Segamat (133).

Selepas beberapa hari reda, beberapa kawasan di Malaysia Timur mula mencatatkan bacaan IPU tidak sihat sekali lagi, iaitu Sri Aman (172), Serian (154) dan Samarahan (129) di Sarawak serta Tawau (154) di Sabah.

Pahang mencatatkan bacaan IPU tidak sihat sebanyak 161 di Balok Baru dan 157 di Rompin, manakala tiga kawasan di Melaka turut melaporkan keadaan serupa, iaitu Bukit Rambai (160), bandar Melaka (160) dan Alor Gajah (151).
Di Negeri Sembilan, bacaan IPU ialah 154 di Seremban dan 146 di Nilai.
Lembah Klang mencatatkan bacaan IPU pada tahap sederhana, walaupun beberapa kawasan menghampiri tahap tidak sihat, iaitu Putrajaya (99), Johan Setia (90) dan Klang (87).
Bacaan IPU 0-50 menunjukkan kualiti udara baik, 51-100 sederhana, 101-200 tidak sihat, 201-300 sangat tidak sihat dan lebih 300 dikategorikan bahaya.

16e1e3b425055538: BEONUS AIRES: Fear of overflowing rivers forced Argentine authorities to temporarily block tourist access to the breathtaking Iguazu Falls on Monday, attributing rising water levels to the El Nino weather pattern.
National park officials took the precautionary measure when the Iguazu River's flow exceeded 12,000 cubic meters per second - more than six times its average rate.
"A temporary restriction on the movement of people and access to public areas has been put in place," Iguazu National Park announced.
It later said the area would reopen to tourists on Tuesday, citing a "gradual decline" in the river's flow.
The northeastern park closed over flooding caused by a previous El Nino cycle in 2023 and 2024.
UN experts have predicted an exceptionally strong cycle of the climate phenomenon, which causes global changes in winds and rainfall as well as erratic weather conditions.
Last month, Argentina's coastal region experienced above-average rainfall "similar to that seen during strong El Nino events," the national meteorological service noted.
The Parana River's flow exceeded historical averages by 37% in September, and by 40% so far in October, a hydroelectric plant on the Paraguayan border said Monday.
Dozens of people living on the banks of the Uruguay River evacuated their homes due to flooding along the major waterway, according to local press reports.
0329ec5a0565247e: NEW YORK: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday after climbing by nearly US$2 a barrel in the previous session, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.
Brent crude futures fell 61 cents, or 0.57 per cent, to US$106.04 a barrel by 0000 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down 47 cents, or 0.5 per cent, at US$93.27 a barrel.
Brent futures settled at US$106.65 a barrel on Monday, the highest since September 15.

US President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to supply ​diesel to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its ‌war on Ukraine.
Additional supplies could help alleviate tightness in global fuel markets, tempering some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices recently.
However, lawmakers from both parties in the US complained Trump's agreement with Putin appears to violate US law barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.

"Fresh diesel supply from Russia and steadier Saudi flows are offering some relief, yet the market still looks more worried about the risk of further hits to ships or pipelines in the Gulf than it is reassured by extra barrels," Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst, said.
"Until we see clearer signs of de-escalation, the path of least resistance still leans higher," he said.

Concerns over the vulnerability of Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping lanes remained in focus after Iran-aligned Houthis struck Riyadh's international airport over the weekend, while tanker attacks were reported near the Strait of Hormuz.

The incidents threatened to derail a recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, and have reinforced fears of further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.

Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels of over one-third of the commodity value, impeding efficient movement of crude oil and products.

OPEC has revised down its oil demand growth forecast for this year to 400,000 barrels per day from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, in line with developments throughout the year, Haitham Al Ghais, Secretary General of the organisation said on Monday.
77b419937f8dca0b: STEPPING behind the camera for her directorial debut was always going to be a steep learning curve for Liyana Jasmay — and choosing horror for her first film brought a wholly different set of challenges.
At 38, Liyana is far more accustomed to being in front of the camera, having spent years establishing herself as an actor.
The singer and producer first entered the entertainment industry as a child actor in 1997.
She achieved widespread recognition and critical acclaim for her roles in films like 'KAMI The Movie' and 'Papadom', the latter earning her Best Actress at the 2009 Malaysian Film Festival.
Directing 'Pemuja Syaitan', however, required her to take responsibility for every single aspect of the production and focus on the bigger picture.
"This is my first experience directing a film and there were so many things I learned throughout the filming process.

"As an actor, we usually focus on our own character, but as a director, I had to look at the entire production, including the acting, camera, storyline, the emotions in every scene and how everything can come together."
NEWBIE DIRECTOR
The transition proved particularly demanding because horror is a genre where fear cannot simply be manufactured through sudden scares.
For Liyana, the real test was creating an atmosphere that would draw audiences in.
"A horror film has its own challenges because we don't just want to shock the audience. We want them to enter the world of the story and feel the fear experienced by the characters."
"That meant there were many things I had to think about on set, including how a particular scene should be performed so that the emotions and atmosphere could reach the audience."
If making the movie was a new test in itself, filming on location in Cherating, Pahang, added an extra layer of mystery.
Liyana says several strange incidents occurred at the site, which had been abandoned.
These unexplainable events were felt not just by her, but also her sister and the production crew.
The team had already been warned about the state of the location, an area rarely visited even by locals.
Even so, experiencing strange occurrences while filming a horror movie naturally put everyone on edge.
"There were several incidents during filming. The location we used had been abandoned for a long time and even the villagers rarely went into the area.
"So, when we arrived to shoot there, we had already been told about the condition of the place. What happened afterwards made us even more careful."
STRANGE ENCOUNTERS
One particular incident left a lasting impression on Liyana.
The Kuantan-born mother of two claims that an unsettling feeling followed her off the set.
"I experienced something quite frightening myself. I saw something like a black figure, perhaps a 'hantu raya', and it felt as if it followed me all the way back to the hotel."
Rather than letting fear take over, Liyana turned to her faith to stay calm.
"I prayed and recited the Quran. After that, I tried to practise certain recitations as often as possible and not think too much about what had happened."
Despite the eerie occurrences, Liyana never thought about stopping production.
"I didn't want us to focus on things like that because when we talk about them too much, we can end up becoming even more afraid.
"So I chose to act as though nothing had happened and continued focusing on the filming. What mattered was that everyone took care of themselves and made their own preparations."
PROTECTING CAST AND CREW
As a precaution, the production team brought in an ustaz (religious teacher).
Even so, Liyana made sure to remind the cast and crew to not let their guard down.
"I told everyone to be prepared. Even though an ustaz was with us, we still had to take our own steps to protect ourselves."
The ustaz advised the team to keep their focus on filming while maintaining their religious practices.
For Liyana, the experience taught her one of the most valuable lessons of directing.
"As a director, I have to think about everyone. It's not just about the film, but also the condition of the actors and crew.
"This is my first film as a director, so there are many experiences I will carry with me into future projects."
UNSETTLING REALITY
Liyana also revealed an even creepier dimension to the shoot.
"In the film, audiences can see for themselves a scene where one of the actors was genuinely 'possessed'.
At the time, the actor was acting but was also already possessed.
"I'm confident audiences will be able to feel that aura because when I was editing the film, I could feel that there was 'something' within the actor."
Whether seen as genuine paranormal encounters or simply part of the superstitious lore that often surrounds horror films, 'Pemuja Syaitan' has given Liyana far more than her first credit as director.
It has tested her leadership, storytelling and sense of responsibility.
Produced by Mermaid Studios in collaboration with Suraya Filem Production & Distribution, 'Pemuja Syaitan' stars Zul Ariffin, Elizabeth Tan, Nadhir Nasar and Aila Azizul.
The film follows a group of school-leavers who reunite in their coastal hometown island.
Their nostalgic gathering takes a dark and terrifying turn after they dig up an old time capsule, accidentally triggering dark rituals, rising tensions and long-buried secrets.
'Pemuja Syaitan' screens in cinemas nationwide from Oct 15.

897bb43c0f5c40a8: CHINESE qualifier Han Shi closed Monday's opening day of action with a 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 upset of 13th-seeded Alexandra Eala of the Philippines at the Wuhan Open in China.

Ranked No. 217 in the world, Shi saved two of three break points and finished with a 31-20 advantage in winners in a match that lasted 2 hours and 27 minutes. Eala had six double faults and 37 unforced errors.

Shi won four consecutive games to close out the second set and raced to a 4-1 lead in the third set. Her opponent in the second round of the WTA 1000 tournament will be Canada's Leylah Fernandez, a 6-4, 3-6, 6-3 winner against Ekaterina Alexandrova of Russia.

No. 15 Jasmine Paolini of Italy was the only other seeded player in action on Monday. She overcame seven double faults by saving eight of 12 break points in a 6-3, 6-4 win against Sara Bejlek of the Czech Republic.
Paolini converted six of 15 break chances and finished with an even 26 winners and 26 unforced errors, compared to 17 and 24 for Bejlek.
American Caty McNally rallied for a 2-6, 7-6 (2), 6-4 victory against Ukraine's Yuliia Starodubtseva.
The other first-round matches were all decided in straight sets, including Xiyu Wang's 6-2, 6-0 win against Chinese compatriot Xinyu Wang in 68 minutes.
Maria Sakkari of Greece defeated Croatia's Donna Vekic 6-4, 6-2. Poland's Magdalena Frech was a 6-3, 7-6 (5) winner over Thailand's Mananchaya Sawangkaew.

Slovakia's Mia Pohankova posted a 6-1, 6-3 win over Anna Bondar of Hungary. Indonesia's Janice Tjen took down Japan's Aoi Ito 6-3, 6-1. Czech Marie Bouzkova was leading 6-1, 2-0 when Denmark's Clara Tauson retired.
Britain's Sonay Kartal beat Ukraine's Anhelina Kalinina 7-5, 6-3. Thailand's Lanlana Tararudee won 6-4, 6-1 against France's Diane Parry.
The tournament's top seeds are No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus and No. 2 Jessica Pegula. World No. 1 Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan and defending champion Coco Gauff withdrew before the tourney.
Sabalenka won the Wuhan title in 2018, 2019 and 2024.

"I feel when you come to the place where you have a lot of success, you feel different," she told reporters at the event's media day. "You feel at home, you feel comfortable with the conditions and with everything here. I definitely feel warm here in Wuhan." — REUTERS
1766199a6aca7371: PETALING JAYA: The financial assistance and other benefits in the 2027 federal budget could improve public sentiment towards Pakatan Harapan, but may not translate into votes at the next general election (GE16), analysts say.
Awang Azman Pawi of Universiti Malaya said public sentiment could shift with the cost of living, economic performance, leadership integrity and political developments.
"In politics, appreciation for government policies does not necessarily mean loyalty to the ruling party," he told FMT.

He said Barisan Nasional had rolled out similar initiatives during its time in government, including BR1M cash aid, Kedai Rakyat 1Malaysia groceries, and setting up one-stop urban transformation centres.
“But it did not guarantee the people’s support, and it even lost the general election,” he said, referring to 2018 when the grand coalition lost power for the first time.
Although the 2027 budget is a government initiative, the finance ministry is helmed by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman.
With the next general election due by February 2028, the 2027 budget could be Anwar’s final budget before voters head to the polls should he call an early election.

The 2027 budget, described by some as an “election budget”, provides for RM460 billion in expenditure, an increase of almost 10% from the 2026 budget, and offers a range of measures aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures and boosting disposable incomes.
Tawfik Yaakub, also of UM, said the measures could boost support, particularly among direct recipients, but the effect could be temporary if households continue to face cost-of-living pressures.

"I expect those in the B40 low-income group, civil servants, government pensioners, young voters and families with school-going children to respond most positively," he said. "This is because the announced benefits address their day-to-day financial needs. However, receiving assistance does not automatically translate into political support."
He said government supporters might view the measures as evidence that the administration cared about the people, while critical voters might see them as a political strategy ahead of GE16.
"Ultimately, public perceptions will depend on the transparency of implementation and the extent to which people genuinely feel the benefits," he said.
Tawfik said the measures could also draw some fence-sitters, but this would again depend on broader economic conditions, including prices, wages and job opportunities.
d3431f355f0f1768: PETALING JAYA: Bantuan kewangan dan manfaat lain dalam Belanjawan 2027 mampu meningkatkan sentimen awam terhadap Pakatan Harapan (PH), namun belum tentu diterjemahkan kepada undi pada PRU16, kata penganalisis.
Awang Azman Pawi daripada Universiti Malaya (UM) berkata, sentimen awam boleh berubah mengikut kos sara hidup, prestasi ekonomi, integriti kepimpinan, dan perkembangan politik.
“Dalam politik, penghargaan terhadap dasar kerajaan tidak semestinya bermakna kesetiaan buat parti pemerintah,” katanya kepada FMT.

Beliau berkata, Barisan Nasional (BN) pernah melaksanakan inisiatif sama ketika menjadi kerajaan, termasuk bantuan tunai BR1M, barangan runcit Kedai Rakyat 1Malaysia, dan penubuhan pusat transformasi bandar setempat.
“Tetapi, ia tidak menjamin sokongan rakyat, malah mereka kalah pada PRU,” katanya merujuk PRU 2018 apabila gabungan itu hilang tampuk kuasa buat julung kali.
Walaupun Belanjawan 2027 inisiatif kerajaan, Kementerian Kewangan diterajui Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim yang juga pengerusi PH.
Memandangkan PRU seterusnya perlu diadakan menjelang Februari 2028, Belanjawan 2027 mungkin menjadi belanjawan terakhir Anwar, jika beliau memanggil pilihan raya awal.

Belanjawan 2027 yang disifatkan sesetengah pihak sebagai 'belanjawan pilihan raya', memperuntukkan belanja RM460 bilion — peningkatan hampir 10% berbanding Belanjawan 2026 — selain menawarkan pelbagai langkah bertujuan meringankan tekanan kos sara hidup dan meningkatkan pendapatan boleh guna.

Tawfik Yaakub yang juga daripada UM berkata, langkah itu boleh meningkatkan sokongan, terutama dalam kalangan penerima secara langsung, namun kesannya mungkin bersifat sementara jika isi rumah terus berdepan tekanan kos sara hidup.

“Saya jangkakan mereka yang berada dalam kumpulan berpendapatan rendah B40, penjawat awam, pesara kerajaan, pengundi muda, dan keluarga yang mempunyai anak bersekolah akan memberikan maklum balas paling positif.
“Ini kerana manfaat diumumkan menangani keperluan kewangan harian mereka. Tetapi, bantuan diterima tidak secara automatik diterjemahkan kepada sokongan politik," katanya.

Beliau berkata, penyokong kerajaan dijangka melihat pendekatan diambil bukti pentadbiran prihatin terhadap rakyat, manakala pengundi yang bersikap kritikal mungkin menganggapnya sebagai strategi politik menjelang PRU16.
“Akhirnya, persepsi awam akan bergantung kepada ketelusan pelaksanaan dan sejauh mana rakyat benar-benar merasai manfaatnya,” katanya.

Tawfik berkata, inisiatif diperkenalkan juga mampu menarik minat sebahagian pengundi atas pagar, namun perkara itu sekali lagi bergantung kepada keadaan meluas ekonomi, termasuk harga barangan, gaji, dan peluang kerja.
4f1ad8660bbb76e4: KUALA LUMPUR: You walk into a room and forget why you’re there. You struggle to recall a familiar name. You read the same line three times, yet nothing registers.
It’s normal to experience moments like these occasionally. But for some people, difficulty in focusing, frequent forgetfulness and persistent mental sluggishness are part of everyday life.
This phenomenon is known as “brain fog”, an informal term to describe a collection of cognitive symptoms that can leave you feeling mentally clouded, distracted and unable to think clearly.

While medical experts clarify that “brain fog” is not a scientific or medical term, the symptoms can feel very real. According to University of Malaya Professor of Geriatric Medicine Dr Tan Maw Pin, the term gained greater recognition during the pandemic.

“Brain fog is not an actual medical diagnosis. But many people who contracted Covid-19 found their brains feeling less sharp after they emerged from the isolation of the illness,” Tan told FMT Lifestyle.
“Their rationale was that the illness had affected the ability of the brain to function, something we call cognitive impairment.”

She explained that this cognitive impairment was connected with a phenomenon known as neuroinflammation, an inflammatory response within the brain and immune response of the central nervous system that can occur in relation to injury, infection, toxins, or disease.

This can lead to the deterioration and loss of brain cells, potentially increasing one’s risk of developing neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s. Scientists are still researching its relationship with other cognitive conditions, including delirium.
Pharmacist Benjamin Lim said brain fog was connected with the brain needing more time to retrieve and process information.

“Imagine your brain is a library. All the information is there. But due to alcohol, stress or lack of sleep, things become messy and muddled up. So, it takes longer to find what you need in the brain,” Lim said.

Tan added that the symptoms associated with brain fog are more likely to occur among older adults and those living with chronic diseases. Despite this, loss of cognitive function can happen to anyone.
Does increased screen time raise the risk of brain fog?

Tan said science had yet to establish a direct link between screen usage and cognitive impairment. However, spending more time on screens could contribute to greater social isolation, which may, in turn, affect mental health.

“We do find a lot of older people are using smartphones as a replacement for their social lives nowadays. Some of them are addicted to just watching videos or sending WhatsApp messages, which increases isolation,” Tan noted.
Lim, meanwhile, added that heavy reliance on technology results in many constantly switching from one device to another, affecting their concentration and cognitive wellbeing.
To help detect and manage chronic conditions associated with brain fog, Tan recommends scheduling regular health screenings.

Meanwhile, maintaining a healthy diet helps reduce the risk of cognitive problems associated with brain fog. Tan recommends eating foods rich in antioxidants and nutrients, such as papaya, sweet potatoes and fish oil.

Antioxidants help protect cells from damage caused by free radicals and oxidative stress. A balanced diet also supports neuroplasticity, or the brain’s ability to adapt and form new neural connections.
Next is regular exercise: Tan recommends at least 150 minutes a week, with resistance training. And lastly, keep the mind mentally stimulated.
“There’s a popular belief that once we leave education, we stop learning new things. That is not right. We need to practise lifelong learning to ensure our minds stay active,” Tan said.

Social participation is yet another factor in maintaining cognitive health. Tan encourages people to remain socially active by regularly meeting with friends and family, participating in community activities, or pursuing hobbies and interests that involve interacting with others.
Ideally, she said, older people should engage in social activities at least twice a week to help keep their minds active and maintain meaningful connections.
If taking supplements to help with mental clarity, Tan cautioned that brands and dosage must be considered carefully.
Look for EGb 761, a standardised, patented extract of ginkgo biloba leaves, recommended for use in dementia, mild cognitive impairment and dizziness.
“It does tend to be true that our brains lose mental sharpness as we age. However, if we maintain healthy lifestyles, we can still live quality lives for a long time,” Tan concluded.
83720383154693d6: ISTANBUL: Barcelona coach Hansi Flick said he would be happy with a single goal victory at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday as his team face one of the world's 'best atmospheres'.
The Catalan giants have won all nine games they have played this season across all competitions, scoring 39 goals, more than four a game on average.
However the visit to face Turkish champions Galatasaray in Istanbul is the first in a string of tougher fixtures for Barcelona, with Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid also coming up.
The Spanish champions thrashed Feyenoord 5-1 in their league phase opener but will be without Raphinha for the visit to Turkey and one of the game's most intimidating environments.
"First of all, we have to be ready for this atmosphere," Flick told reporters Monday.
"I think this is one of the best atmospheres ever in the world. It's amazing when I hear some situations or the sounds of the stadium, what the fans are doing, it's unbelievable.
"They support their team. You also can see the results against big teams, they are playing like a big team against them, they've improved a lot."
Not since Barcelona's 2-0 win over Athletic Bilbao in La Liga on August 27 have the Catalans been restricted to fewer than three goals.
However Flick said just one would do at Galatasaray's hostile Rams Park stadium, which has sometimes been nicknamed "Hell."
"The only thing we want is to win, this is our goal, this is what we want," said Flick.
"I'm also happy if we win just 1-0, because to see this team, how they play, how they play out (from the back), they like to play football.
"In attack they have fantastic players, so it's not easy to play against Galatasaray, especially at home."--AFP
d6f0b0a482c0ac39: KUALA LUMPUR: Children born to Malaysian Malays and foreign Muslim spouses can be registered as Malays, provided they are born from a marriage recognised under Malaysian law, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the parents could choose to register the child's ethnicity according to either the Malaysian parent's Malay ethnicity or the foreign parent's ethnicity.
However, Saifuddin said marriage to a Malaysian of Malay descent did not change the foreign spouse's ethnicity, which would remain unchanged.
"The National Registration Department would not determine the ethnicity of the foreign spouse.

"The determination of whether a person qualified as a Bumiputera and was eligible for the rights or privileges accorded to the group also fell outside the department's jurisdiction, as such matters were subject to the laws, policies and conditions set by the relevant agencies or authorities," he said in a parliamentary written reply.

Saifuddin was responding to a question from Labis MP Pang Hok Liong, who asked whether foreign Muslims married to Malaysians of Malay descent could be considered Bumiputera and enjoy the rights and privileges accorded to the group, as well as the conditions involved.
49c59b71bff1a74b: NEW YORK: US actress Selma Blair was arrested after an alleged altercation on a flight from Los Angeles to New York City that injured at least two cabin crew members, authorities said Monday.
The "Legally Blonde" and "Cruel Intentions" star was detained at John F Kennedy Airport after her Delta Air Lines flight landed late Sunday following reports of a physically abusive passenger.
US media said that Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another. The 54-year-old then reportedly assaulted a police officer and nurse as she was transported to hospital.
"Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," a representative for Blair said.
"Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."
The FBI issued a summons accusing Blair of assaults on the plane, according to a federal judicial source.
A spokesperson for Delta said the airline "has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behaviour, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first."
In 2016, Blair was removed from a plane on a stretcher after another outburst on a flight.
"I mixed alcohol with medication, and that caused me to black out and led me to say and do things that I deeply regret," she told Vanity Fair after that incident.
She also described in her 2022 memoir having bitten several celebrities, including Kate Moss, often in situations where she had been drinking alcohol.--AFP
2c7c27f113d36c4c: NEW YORK: US stock indexes were a mixed bag on Monday as oil prices touched their highest in almost two weeks and technology stocks fell as investors waited for third-quarter earnings season and a raft of key economic releases due later this week.
US crude futures jumped more than 2.0 per cent and Brent futures were above US$106 a barrel after deadly strikes on Riyadh's international airport over the weekend.
The attacks overshadowed the prospect of increased supplies after US President Donald Trump hailed fresh Russian diesel exports and talked about a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy targets.
In coming days, investors will focus on corporate earnings, with major US banks including Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and JPMorgan Chase reporting early on Tuesday.
S&P 500 earnings were expected to surge 30.6 per cent in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

Also due this week are September readings for US consumer and producer inflation data as well as retail sales data. While the US Treasury market was closed on Monday for Columbus Day, stock investors have been wary of bond yields' recent advance to 24-year highs as elevated energy prices have stoked inflation concerns.

"Looking out further in the week, we have some big economic reports," said Tim Ghriskey, senior portfolio strategist at Ingalls & Snyder in New York. He said investors were cautious due to a lack of direction from bonds.
"We're also waiting on earnings and that's significant. The four large banks reporting on Tuesday can have a big impact," he said.

At 02:16 pm ET (1816 GMT) the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 175.51 points, or 0.34 per cent, to 51,830.46, the S&P 500 lost 10.51 points, or 0.13 per cent, to 7,801.03 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 126.08 points, or 0.46 per cent, to 27,240.09.

With oil prices rising, energy was the biggest gainer among the S&P 500's 11 major industry sectors, up 1.4 per cent. S&P 500 communication services notched the next biggest advance, up 1.3 per cent, with a boost from Meta, which added more than 4.0 per cent.

Technology and consumer discretionary were the only two sectors in the red. Technology was the biggest decliner, down roughly 1.0 per cent with weakness most pronounced among chip stocks. The Philadelphia semiconductor index was down 2.6 per cent after hitting a three-week low.
Consumer discretionary was down 0.6 per cent. One of its top losers was Chipotle Mexican Grill, down 5.0 per cent after Starbucks said it was not buying the burrito chain.
Microsoft was up 0.9 per cent. Earlier its market capitalization rose above US$4 trillion for the first time in a year following its announcement of plans for a major deployment of its own AI chips.

Salesforce shares rose 1.3 per cent after BofA Global Research upgraded the stock to "buy" from "underperform." EBay gained more than 4 per cent after Morgan Stanley added the stock to its top-pick list.

Meanwhile, Cleveland Federal Reserve President Beth Hammack said on Monday the US central bank should move "relatively quickly" to a restrictive monetary policy stance to fight inflation, which she feels has become more broad-based and is starting to influence firms' price-setting plans.
Markets are pricing in just a 19 per cent chance the US Federal Reserve will raise interest rates this month, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.01-to-1 ratio on the NYSE where there were 122 new highs and 214 new lows.

On the Nasdaq, 1,866 stocks rose and 2,828 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.52-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 10 new 52-week highs and 5 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 47 new highs and 277 new lows.
